Storage: designed assets saved as asset@1 files under `.axf-console/plugins/asset-designer/assets/<type>/<id>.json` (lifecycle dataDir), served by `GET /api/plugins/asset-designer/assets`, registered into the runtime on load like the theme-manager plugin does (`registry.register`, origin `asset-designer`). Built-in ids refused.

Menu editor (nav-menu, app-menu, context-menu): tree of items (label, icon, action, children, divider), drag to reorder, action picker from `rt.actions.list()`, live preview via `rt.swap` on a `ad-preview-<type>` id. Reuses `MenuList.tsx` for the preview.

Toolbar editor: items (icon, label, action, badge counter), `density`/`surface`/`divider`/`collapsible`, widgets start/end picker from `attachable` types (engine-rpc `app-defaults` → `widgets`), live preview through the React `Toolbar`.

`drawer` asset type: add it to `asset-types.json` (hideable chrome, `side` left/right, `width`, `items` like nav-menu, `modal`), `layout.slots` accept it in the `drawer` region, starter `framework/assets/drawer/amberx-side.json`, `framework/defaults.json` names it. Validators on all three ports accept it (Kotlin: `AssetTypeSpec` resource); fixture case in `layout-slots.json`.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

before.title: Asset Browser plugin
before.detail: Browse, preview, import, export and hot-swap assets across apps built on AXF. Installed by default.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Plugin skeleton `apps/console-web/plugins/asset-browser` from `_template` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-browser`, lifecycle, install/uninstall, nav → Plugins → Asset browser, settings sub-tab). Lifecycle check + console build pass.

Sources: server route `GET /api/plugins/asset-browser/sources` lists asset folders it may read: framework starters (`framework/assets`), every app under `apps/*/src/assets` or `app/src/main/assets/axf` (from `framework/cli/app-bundle.mjs list`), designed assets (asset-designer dataDir when present). Never follows symlinks; roots only.
Browse view: grid by type → source → asset, search box (reuses `consoleSearch.ts` provider pattern), type chips from `asset-types.json`, counts per source. Rows show id, label, origin, tier.

Preview: `AssetPreview.tsx` from `framework/react/studio` renders the selected asset in a card; for chrome types a live preview on an `ab-preview-<type>` swap like theme-manager; "Apply here" = `rt.swap(type, id)` after `registry.register`.

Import: drop/paste JSON or pick a file → `validateAsset` → preview → install into a chosen target (console runtime, or an app folder through `POST /api/plugins/asset-browser/install {source, target, type, id}` that writes the file only inside allowed app asset folders; built-in ids refused; backups under the plugin dataDir).

Export: single asset or a pack (zip of asset@1 files + `pack.json`), served by `GET …/export?ids=`; packs are what the plugin runtime (`x.plugins`, PACK kind) will load later, so write the `pack@1` shape now in `framework/schemas/asset-pack.json`.

Hot-swap across apps: for apps running `axf dev` (`framework/cli/dev-server.mjs`), "Push to device" posts the asset to the dev server's folder so the HotReloader picks it up; list dev servers from settings (`axf.devServer`). Error card when none.

Installed by default + Android: enabled in console plugin defaults, `plugins.json` catalog entry, `plugins.mjs --check`; Android `axf-devtools` route `asset-browser` showing the bundled assets by type with Apply (uses `AssetRegistry` + `AxfRuntime.swap`), so Settings → Plugins lists it on both ports.
Tests: `test.py` (sources never leave roots, import validation, built-in refusal, export pack shape), lifecycle check, CI line.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-browser.md` + LOG.md + web screenshots, CLAUDE.md Status, plan `x.assets.browser` built, pending complete.

before.title: Plugin manager + settings tabs for every app (Fable rebuild)
before.detail: Every plugin gets a plugin-manager entry (info, enable/disable, view logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen; they add tabs to the app settings interface. Every app compiled by the build engine ships the settings interface and lib-settings. The Opus version is the console plugin `plugin-manager` (web console only: four views cards/table/detail/dependency graph in four layouts Studio/Mission control/Terminal/Catalog, default context-menu link, dependencies in detail, opens each plugin's UI and settings, logs, files, install & uninstall). Remove it first with its uninstall script (uninstall.mjs --all --publish), then build the cross-port version following plugin-lifecycle@1 (Android kernel + every app the build engine compiles), keeping the UI-editor rules (last save wins per key; reload current values on open/load/focus).

notes.text: Opus console plugin `plugin-manager` built Oct 18 2026. Remove with its uninstall.mjs --all before installing the Fable build.
Fable rebuild done Oct 20 2026 on branch fable/plugin-manager. Differences report: _claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/plugin-manager.md
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

before.title: Asset templates: 10+ per type + defaults
before.detail: At least 10 editable templates/boilerplates for every asset type the designer covers, plus a default asset per type.

notes.text: Overlaps settings-asset (new `settings` asset type, branch claude/project-thread-55oakl); build with settings-asset-fable.
Nov 3 2026: Build Pilot is retired; s13 only covers the console's asset designer now.
Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Template index: `framework/assets/templates/index.json` (`asset-templates@1`: id, type, label, tags, file) + loader `listAssetTemplates(type)` in `framework/cli/build-engine.mjs`; engine-rpc `asset-templates`, console `GET /api/asset-templates?type=`. Empty list works end to end.

Validation in CI: `framework/spec/check-asset-templates.mjs` loads every template, runs `validateAsset`, checks unique ids, ≥ 10 per covered type once a type is marked `complete` in the index, and that each type has a `default`. Wire into `android.yml` (node job).

nav-menu ×10: side nav, bottom tabs, rail, grouped sections, icon-only, with badges, two-level, settings-first, admin, minimal. Each a valid `nav-menu` asset in `framework/assets/templates/nav-menu/`.
app-menu ×10 (file/edit/view style menus, single-page apps, tool apps…) + context-menu ×10 (text, list row, card, media, dev, file, link, minimal, with submenus, keyboard hints).
toolbar ×10: editor, media, search-first, compact icons, labelled, split start/end with widgets, status-heavy (counters/progress), collapsible, roomy, minimal.
layout ×10: dashboard, master-detail, sidebar-left/right, bottom-nav phone, kiosk, editor + inspector, chat, settings, full-bleed, three-pane. Each with `data.slots` where it narrows a region.
drawer ×10 (needs `asset-designer` step 7's `drawer` type): left/right, modal/non-modal, wide/narrow, with header, grouped, icon rail, account-first, admin, minimal.

color-theme ×10 light + ×10 dark (pairs): contrast-checked with `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks run from a script; names in one family (`arctic-daylight` style). Each pair shares a `pair` tag.
style-theme ×10: glass, flat, outlined, dense, roomy, rounded, square, hairline, soft, print. Numbers inside ranges known themes use; every opacity token present.

Defaults: `framework/defaults.json` + `framework/app-defaults.json` reviewed so every type has a default template id (new field `templates.default.<type>` read by `axf init` for "start from a template"); `axf init --template-set <id>` option registered in `build-options.json` only if it sets a token, else as an init argument.

Previews: `framework/cli/rebuild-shots.mjs`-style script `framework/cli/template-shots.mjs` renders each template in the demo app headless (phone + desktop) to `framework/assets/templates/<type>/shots/`; `index.json` entries get `shot`. Run once; commit shots ≤ 60 KB each (`framework/cli/shrink-shots.py`).

Android: templates bundled into `axf-assets` as a resource folder so Compose previews (`ComponentGallery.kt`) and the future Android designer read the same files; `AssetTemplates` Kotlin loader + a unit test that every bundled template validates.

Hooks: asset-designer "Start from" and Build Pilot's designers list templates by type (console `GET /api/asset-templates`); asset-browser shows a Templates source. Add the `templates` capability to `app-defaults` engine-rpc.
Close: regenerate fixtures touched (`gen-fixtures.mts`), CI green, report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-templates.md`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan `x.assets.templates` built, pending complete.

before.title: Libraries: settings, logging, admin, accounts, profile, billing
before.detail: The six libraries the console and apps build on. Settings and logging are complete; accounts and billing run on mock providers.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Scope note first: `_claude/memory/docs/libs-core.md` — for each of admin, accounts, profile, billing: what the Android placeholder has (`lib-admin`, `lib-accounts`, `lib-profile`, `lib-billing` screens + modules), what "real" means per port (accounts = axHub provider from `x.session`; billing = provider interface only, Play Billing as a separate library per the plan's recommendation), the web library ids (`ai.amberx.axf.<name>`).

Web lib-logging: `framework/libs/logging` (`AxfWebLibrary`: log sinks via `ExtensionPoints.LOG_SINKS`, levels, the Output terminal as default sink, Settings → General → Logging group) matching `lib-logging` on Android; `axf init` web templates install it beside settings.

Web lib-accounts: `framework/libs/accounts` (Account view = today's `react/studio/AccountView.tsx` moved into the library, sign-in/out through `rt.session` providers, Settings → Account group); the console installs it.

Android lib-accounts real: `AccountsModule` consumes `AUTH_PROVIDERS` (from `x.session` step 4), `AccountScreen` shows the provider's principal, sign-in/out, errors; mock provider moved to `lib-accounts-mock`; `lib-accounts` unit test with a fake provider.

Profile: `lib-profile` Android (`ProfileScreen` edits display name/avatar stored per principal in KV, exported through a `ProfileProvider` interface) + web `framework/libs/profile` (same provider interface, avatar widget uses `avatar` widget kind); contract in `core/profile.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Profile.kt`.

Admin: `lib-admin` Android + web `framework/libs/admin`: an admin-only view (UAC `admin.*`) listing modules/libraries (plugin-inventory), audit log, flags toggles (`x.state` flags), feature kill switches; hidden entirely without the role.

Billing: provider contract `core/billing.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Billing.kt` (products, entitlements, purchase flow result, restore), `BILLING_PROVIDERS` typed; `lib-billing` Android with a `NoBilling` provider (entitlements empty) and `SubscriptionScreen` driven by the provider; web `framework/libs/billing` same; Play Billing library parked as a plan feature (`x.lib.billing.play`).
Fixtures + Kotlin tests: `spec/fixtures/libs-core.json` (profile validation, billing entitlement rules, admin role gate) replayed on both ports; written without a compiler.
Templates: `axf init` installs logging + accounts + profile on web/Android by default (settings already is), build options unchanged; CI template sweep + `axf validate` on the generated apps.

Catalog + status: `libraries.json` entries for the six on web/android/python(planned), status.json features `a.admin`, `u.accounts`, `p.profile`, `b.subs` → built (billing = contract + NoBilling), tracker, `build_step complete`.

before.title: Import third-party UI libraries → AmberX kits
before.detail: axf import-ui clones (git/local) or records (maven/npm) a library, rewrites literals and Material/MUI roles to AXF tokens, saves kit-<id> + its ui-kit asset and applies it to the open project.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Real-library trial: run `axf import-ui --name Cupertino --kit cupertino --source git --path <compose-cupertino repo>` into a scratch android-compose app (`/tmp`), read `tokens.map.json`, list what the codemod missed (patterns + counts) in `_claude/memory/docs/uiport-trial.md`.

Codemod fixes from the trial: extend `ROLE_MAP`/`guessToken` in `framework/cli/ui-port.mjs` for the missed Compose patterns (e.g. `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.x`, `Modifier.padding(Nn.dp)` → space tokens), unit cases in `framework/spec/check-uiport.mjs` (new; fixture snippets in `spec/fixtures/uiport/`).

Kit overrides: generated `kit-<id>` module gets per-kind override files from the library's components (mapping table in `tokens.map.json` → `components.map.json`), default components kept where unmapped; the ui-kit asset lists `covers`.
Web side: `import-ui` for npm libraries (MUI first) generating `framework/libs/kit-<id>` from the `ui-kit` library template with the same maps; `check-theme.mjs` passes on the output.
CI + status: `check-uiport.mjs` in `android.yml` (node job) + the existing fake-lib import sweep; plan warnings cleared, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`.

before.title: Live reload (axf dev) + device hot reload
before.detail: axf dev watches assets and long-polls changes to devices; the Android HotReloader re-registers changed assets live.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Web hot reload: `framework/react` `useDevServer(url)` long-polls `/events` from `dev-server.mjs` and re-registers changed assets (`registry.register` + `rt.refreshFromSaved`); `axf dev` prints the URL; demo app opts in with `?axfDev=`.

Android end to end on the emulator (CI): `rebuild-shots.yml`-style job step that starts `axf dev --framework` on the runner, points the emulator at `10.0.2.2:7070` (setting `axf.devServer`, flag `axf.hotReload`), edits a theme file, screenshots before/after and asserts the pixel diff > 0.

Robustness: dev server validates every changed file before announcing it (invalid → `/events` carries `error` and the device shows a terminal line), ignores editor temp files, handles rename/delete; `check-dev-server.mjs` test with a temp folder.
Docs + status: README section "Live reload on a phone" (PC IP, same Wi-Fi), plan warning cleared, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`.

before.title: Session, principal, audit log
before.detail: Session/Principal/SessionProvider contracts and an AuditLog service; accounts library uses a mock auth provider.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Web contract: `framework/core/session.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Session.kt` (`Principal`, `Session`, `SessionState`, `SessionProvider`, `AnonymousSession`, `AuditEntry`, `AuditLog`, `MemoryAuditLog`); `rt.session` replaces the ad-hoc principal in `runtime.ts` (`bindPrincipal` keeps working, built on it); fixture `spec/fixtures/session.json` (state transitions, audit cap).

Audit log everywhere: every UAC-denied action, swap, settings write of a locked key and bound-principal refusal records an `AuditEntry` (web + Kotlin, same action names); Settings → Account & security → **Audit** list (last 100) in `libs/settings` and Android `SettingsScreen`.

Real provider, axHub: `lib-hub` gets `AxhubSessionProvider` (web: `/api/me` + hub cookie; Android: the AXHub app's cookie-jar sign-in) mapping hub role/perms → `Principal`; the console's `account.tsx` reads `rt.session` instead of its own fetch; first non-mock provider.

Kotlin: `AuthProviders` extension point typed (`AUTH_PROVIDERS` → `SessionProvider`), `lib-accounts` picks the first registered provider (mock stays as fallback module `lib-accounts-mock`); `SessionConformanceTest` replays the fixture; written without a compiler.

Persistence: session survives restart (Kotlin KV `<key>:session` minus secrets; web settings), `EXPIRED`/`LOCKED` transitions on expiry and app lock (lib-lock hooks `LOCKED`); fixture cases for expiry.
Tests + CI: `check-session.mts`, Kotlin test, console `test_wall_users.py` unchanged; CI lines.
Docs + status: PORTING.md "Session + audit", plan android/web partial → built, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`; warning "No real sign-in provider yet" cleared.

before.title: Python / PyQt6 port
before.detail: Port the kernel engines to Python, pass the conformance fixtures, add a PyQt6 UI layer, a Qt Widgets kit and a pyqt6 app template.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Plan the port (no code): `_claude/memory/docs/python-port.md` — engines in fixture order (theme → layout → components → UAC → actions → hide/spacing/roll/search → banner/widgets), package layout `framework/python/axf/engines/`, dataclasses mirroring the Kotlin models, how fixtures are replayed (`framework/python/axf/spec/replay.py`), what the PyQt6 layer covers in the first slice.

Fixture replay harness: `framework/python/axf/spec/replay.py` loads every `spec/fixtures/*.json`, dispatches by fixture name to a registered engine, reports pass/fail per case; CI job `python-port` runs it (allowed to skip unported engines, listed).
Asset model + validator: `axf/asset.py` (envelope dataclass, `validate_asset` from `asset-types.json` incl. `attach`/`widgets` hosts, slot checks) replaying `validation.json`.
Theme engine: `axf/engines/theme.py` (color + style compile, spacing scale, opacity tokens) replaying `theme.json` + `spacing.json`.
Layout engine: `axf/engines/layout.py` (`compile_slots`, `region_accepts`, hidden regions) replaying `layout.json`, `layout-slots.json`, `hide.json`.
Components engine: `axf/engines/components.py` (component styles, toolbar/nav/app-menu style inputs, container collapsible, toolbar collapsible) replaying `components.json`.
UAC + actions: `axf/engines/uac.py`, `actions.py` replaying `uac.json`, `actions.json`, `menu-filter.json`.
Roll + search engines: `axf/engines/roll.py`, `search.py` replaying `roll.json`, `search.json`.
Banner + widgets engines: `axf/engines/banner.py`, `widgets.py` (host registry, kinds rules) replaying `banner.json`, `widgets.json`.
Runtime: `axf/runtime.py` (registry, swap, settings store, hidden slots, attachments, bound principal, session from `x.session`) with the same action ids; smoke test registering the starter assets.
Project gate: `axf/project.py` validator replaying `project-manifest.json` (same rules file), used by the pyqt6 template's guard.

PyQt6 shell, part 1: `axf/qt/shell.py` — window with banner, menubar (app-menu), toolbar, nav (side list), content region from the compiled layout; theme tokens → Qt stylesheet via a token→QSS compiler.
PyQt6 shell, part 2: dialogs/popups, context menu, settings window driven by `SettingsGroup`s (lib-settings python), search bar widget, clock widget; hot-swap re-applies QSS live.
Qt Widgets kit: `axf/qt/kit.py` implementing the `ComponentKind` table on QtWidgets through the uikit resolver (`x.uikits` python placeholder becomes real).

Template `pyqt6`: `framework/templates/pyqt6` (`template.json`, `project.manifest.json`, `main.py`, `requirements.txt`, guard), `axf init --template pyqt6` wired in `build-engine.mjs` (bakes `framework/python/axf` + assets); `axf validate` on the output.
Tests + CI: replay harness must pass every fixture (no skips left), `python -m pytest framework/python` job, template sweep includes pyqt6 (no display: `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` smoke).
Docs + status: PORTING.md "Python port", plan python ports → built across epics touched, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`; `axf init` README lists the template.

before.detail: plugin@1 manifest, scopes, action macros and a PluginLoader contract exist; loading plugins at runtime is a placeholder.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Design check (no code): read `contract/Plugin.kt` (PACK/MODULE/SCRIPT, scopes, `PluginLoader`), `framework/schemas/asset-pack.json` if asset-browser made it, and the plugin-catalog format; write `_claude/memory/docs/plugin-runtime.md`: what a PACK may carry (assets, action macros, string packs), install sources (file, URL, QR, console catalog), grants UI, and what stays placeholder (MODULE code loading, SCRIPT).

before.title: Background work scheduler
before.detail: WorkSpec / Worker / WorkRegistry contracts and a placeholder scheduler. Real implementation is WorkManager on Android.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Web contract: `framework/core/work.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Work.kt` (`WorkSpec`, `WorkConstraints`, policies, states, `WorkRegistry` of workers by id); fixture `spec/fixtures/work.json` (unique + KEEP/REPLACE/APPEND rules, backoff computation, constraint evaluation with explicit inputs).

Android scheduler: `axf-platform-android` `WorkManagerScheduler` mapping `WorkSpec` → WorkManager requests (constraints, backoff, unique work policy), `WorkRegistry` dispatch inside one `AxfWorker`; capability `axf.work` real; periodic + one-shot; progress through `WorkState` flow. Written without a compiler.

Web scheduler: `framework/libs/work` with a `setTimeout`/visibility-aware scheduler (one-shot + periodic while the page lives, persisted queue in settings so a reload re-enqueues), constraints evaluated with `navigator.connection`/battery where available, else ignored with a terminal note.

Workers registry: `ExtensionPoints.WORKERS` typed (`WorkerContribution {id, run}`) on Kotlin + web; the alerts library's 3-minute poll becomes the first web worker; Android console showcase registers a demo periodic worker (logs a line).

Docs + status: PORTING.md "Background work", plan android placeholder → built, web → built, features `k.scheduler`/`dv.bg` built, tracker, `build_step complete`.

before.title: Console in its own private repo
before.detail: Split apps/console-web into a private repo that depends on a tagged framework version.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "main-framework" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: BRETT says go (rule: not until he does) and picks the dependency style: tagged framework version via git tag + `npm pack`-style tarball, or a git submodule. Record in decisions.md.

Framework packaging: `framework/cli/axf.mjs pack-framework <tag>` producing `axf-framework-<tag>.tgz` (core, react, ui, schemas, libs, plan cores) + a GitHub release asset on tag push (`release.yml`).

Repo split: create `MossesX/axf-console` (exists on GitHub first), move `apps/console-web` with history (`git subtree split`), manifest `location` + `repo.exists: true`, `_claude/` + CLAUDE.md via `claude-project`; CI there re-bakes from the tagged tarball instead of `../../framework`.

This repo: `apps/console-web` becomes a thin pointer (README + manifest `location` pointing at the new repo), `install-console.sh` clones the console repo; `deploy/` scripts and `android.yml` console job updated.
Verify: console builds in its repo against the tag, deploy on the VPS from the new clone, `/api/health` + `/mcp` ok; status + `build_step complete`.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

after.title: UI Roller: roll a random style on any UI element
after.detail: New UI Roller plugin (console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web; every app built on the framework). 1) Context menu on EVERY UI element (dialogs, windows, panels, bars, buttons, inputs, menus, text, widgets; all registry assets): 'Roll style' and, when the element has a roll, 'Reset element'. 2) 'Roll style' opens a dialog: checkboxes for what to roll (colours, typography, spacing/density, size, radius/shape, borders, shadows, motion, icons), optional scope (this element / all of its type / its plugin), live preview, Re-roll, Apply. Rolls stay within valid token ranges and keep contrast readable. Apply saves the result as asset token overrides (local-first, like other overrides). 3) Main Settings > Rolled assets page: lists every app and plugin with its rolled assets (tree, counts, filters, search); each shows a live preview of the asset and its roll; actions: Reset (one), Reset selected (multi-select), Reset all. Undo/history per roll. 4) Applying a skin, design pack or theme clears EVERY rolled asset: covered ones take the new look, all others go back to their defaults. 5) Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep links for roll, reset, reset selected/all and the page. Stock framework controls; 3 layout options to UI Review; tests (roll writes tokens, reset restores, theme apply clears all rolls); report.

origin.said: I need a UI roller plugin for every single UI element dialog window. Every single UI element needs a roll style. So you pick the context menu and the element you're over, it comes up and you can go roll style. Or reset element, if it's already been changed, and it'll just roll a random style and save it to the tokens. When you click roll, it opens a dialogue, and you can select what things you want in the roll. Every plugin or app, in the main settings there needs to be a rolled assets page that lists all the plugins and any rolled assets so you can view the asset itself in a preview and reset it, reset all, and reset selected. Whenever you apply a skin or a design pack or a theme, it resets the rolled assets; rolled assets that it doesn't touch go back to default before the roll.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

steps.text: Switching the active account actually signs the VPS Claude login in to it (live login matches active), banner clock badge goes live
Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Console approval pop-up: Approve / Deny act in place, never open new browser windows or tabs (find what opens them and stop it)
axHub policy: veto only for calls that write to the VPS or switch Claude accounts; console planner/orchestrator/plan writes and other non-VPS writes run as allow (audited)
Update shared rules + decisions.md, tests

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

steps.text: Switching the active account actually signs the VPS Claude login in to it (live login matches active), banner clock badge goes live
Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.

# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs." Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."
origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: UI Roller: roll a random style on any UI element
before.detail: New UI Roller plugin (console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web; every app built on the framework). 1) Context menu on EVERY UI element (dialogs, windows, panels, bars, buttons, inputs, menus, text, widgets; all registry assets): 'Roll style' and, when the element has a roll, 'Reset element'. 2) 'Roll style' opens a dialog: checkboxes for what to roll (colours, typography, spacing/density, size, radius/shape, borders, shadows, motion, icons), optional scope (this element / all of its type / its plugin), live preview, Re-roll, Apply. Rolls stay within valid token ranges and keep contrast readable. Apply saves the result as asset token overrides (local-first, like other overrides). 3) Main Settings > Rolled assets page: lists every app and plugin with its rolled assets (tree, counts, filters, search); each shows a live preview of the asset and its roll; actions: Reset (one), Reset selected (multi-select), Reset all. Undo/history per roll. 4) Applying a skin, design pack or theme clears EVERY rolled asset: covered ones take the new look, all others go back to their defaults. 5) Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep links for roll, reset, reset selected/all and the page. Stock framework controls; 3 layout options to UI Review; tests (roll writes tokens, reset restores, theme apply clears all rolls); report.

origin.said: I need a UI roller plugin for every single UI element dialog window. Every single UI element needs a roll style. So you pick the context menu and the element you're over, it comes up and you can go roll style. When you click roll, it opens a dialogue, and you can select what things you want in the roll. Every plugin or app, in the main settings there needs to be a rolled assets page that lists all the plugins and any rolled assets so you can view the asset itself in a preview and reset it, reset all, and reset selected. Whenever you apply a skin or a design pack or a theme, it resets the rolled assets; rolled assets that it doesn't touch go back to default before the roll.

after.detail: New UI Roller plugin (console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web; every app built on the framework). 1) Context menu on EVERY UI element (dialogs, windows, panels, bars, buttons, inputs, menus, text, widgets; all registry assets): 'Roll style' and, when the element has a roll, 'Reset element'. 2) 'Roll style' opens a dialog: checkboxes for what to roll (colours, typography, spacing/density, size, radius/shape, borders, shadows, motion, icons), optional scope (this element / all of its type / its plugin), live preview, Re-roll, Apply. Rolls stay within valid token ranges and keep contrast readable. Apply saves the result as asset token overrides (local-first, like other overrides). 3) Main Settings > Rolled assets page: lists every app and plugin with its rolled assets (tree, counts, filters, search); each shows a live preview of the asset and its roll; actions: Reset (one), Reset selected (multi-select), Reset all. Undo/history per roll. 4) Applying a skin, design pack or theme clears EVERY rolled asset: covered ones take the new look, all others go back to their defaults. 5) Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep links for roll, reset, reset selected/all and the page. Stock framework controls; 3 layout options to UI Review; tests (roll writes tokens, reset restores, theme apply clears all rolls); report.

## Brett said (verbatim)
> Make sure it creates the plant studio, make sure it gets all the, the correct information, the fields of the manifest are sent to the plant studio. So the plant studio's gotta receive a manifest too. It has to be valid.

## What to build
Continue build "Plan Studio receives a valid shipped-feature manifest" (plan-studio-receives-a-valid-shipped-feature-man) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"Make sure it creates the plant studio, make sure it gets all the, the correct information, the fields of the manifest are sent to the plant studio. So the plant studio's gotta receive a manifest too. It has to be valid."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Console approval pop-up: Approve / Deny act in place, never open new browser windows or tabs (find what opens them and stop it)
axHub policy: veto only for calls that write to the VPS or switch Claude accounts; console planner/orchestrator/plan writes and other non-VPS writes run as allow (audited)
Update shared rules + decisions.md, tests

before.title: Owner-only settings: Brett's admin console login counts as owner
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> won't let me set it. It says no way enabled by owner only. Only Brett changes it. With his own click in the console. ... I can't click it.
> I'm logged in as admin.

Problem: Settings → Plugins → Claude refuses owner-only switches (No wait) for Brett's signed-in admin console session. Fix the owner check so Brett's own login is recognised as owner. Queue behind the account/badge build (one build at a time).

before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: Briefs list the existing files each step needs
before.detail: Today every orchestrator brief says 'read only the files listed' but lists no files. When the orchestrator splits a build into steps, it looks up the existing files each step will need (plugin folders, plugin.json, server/web entry points, schemas, the CLI/engine files it extends) from the plugin/UI registry, the Shipped features ledger and a quick grep, and writes them into the brief per step as 'Start with these files'. New files are not listed. Keep the list short (the files that matter, not whole folders). Also trim the brief: Brett's words once (not twice), steps, files, how to tick steps; drop boilerplate that doesn't apply to the step (look/token rules only for UI steps). Tests: brief template lists files per step; a UI step gets the look rules, a non-UI step doesn't; Brett's words appear once.

before.title: UI Roller: roll a random style on any UI element
before.detail: New UI Roller plugin (console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web; every app built on the framework). 1) Context menu on EVERY UI element (dialogs, windows, panels, bars, buttons, inputs, menus, text, widgets; all registry assets): 'Roll style' and, when the element has a roll, 'Reset element'. 2) 'Roll style' opens a dialog: checkboxes for what to roll (colours, typography, spacing/density, size, radius/shape, borders, shadows, motion, icons), optional scope (this element / all of its type / its plugin), live preview, Re-roll, Apply. Rolls stay within valid token ranges and keep contrast readable. Apply saves the result as asset token overrides (local-first, like other overrides). 3) Main Settings > Rolled assets page: lists every app and plugin with its rolled assets (tree, counts, filters, search); each shows a live preview of the asset and its roll; actions: Reset (one), Reset selected (multi-select), Reset all. Undo/history per roll. 4) Applying a skin, design pack or theme clears EVERY rolled asset: covered ones take the new look, all others go back to their defaults. 5) Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep links for roll, reset, reset selected/all and the page. Stock framework controls; 3 layout options to UI Review; tests (roll writes tokens, reset restores, theme apply clears all rolls); report.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

origin.said: I need a UI roller plugin for every single UI element dialog window. Every single UI element needs a roll style. So you pick the context menu and the element you're over, it comes up and you can go roll style. Or reset element, if it's already been changed, and it'll just roll a random style and save it to the tokens. When you click roll, it opens a dialogue, and you can select what things you want in the roll. Every plugin or app, in the main settings there needs to be a rolled assets page that lists all the plugins and any rolled assets so you can view the asset itself in a preview and reset it, reset all, and reset selected. Whenever you apply a skin or a design pack or a theme, it resets the rolled assets; rolled assets that it doesn't touch go back to default before the roll.

before.title: URGENT: approval links say 'Method not allowed'
before.detail: Approval links sent in notices and by Claude (https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/admin/approvals/<id>) answer 'Method not allowed' when Brett taps Approve. The hub's plain HTML approval pages were removed when every axhub.amberxai.com route moved to the axhub-web app, so the old link/form posts to a route that no longer takes it. Fix: the approval link opens the approval in axhub-web (or the console) with working Approve/Deny that call the hub's decide API with the right method; keep the old URL working as a redirect. Check every place that builds approval links (notices, AmberX push, console banner, axHub tool results approvalUrl). Test Approve and Deny end to end on a veto hold and a confirm hold. Land it the same day.

after.title: Go-to hooks: every shipped feature, build and plan opens the UI or setting it touched
after.detail: Every Shipped Features entry, build (Pending/Queued/Built) and Plan Studio plan that relates to a UI, screen, dialog, plugin or setting carries go-to hooks. The manifest records the UI targets it touched (view ids, dialogs, settings tabs/keys, plugin, element selectors) from the registry. In the row: an 'Open' button (opens the main target), and in the expanded row a 'Go to' list of every target. Clicking opens it in the console (or Molly/AmberX) via deep link / console_show, focused, scrolled into view, centered and highlighted. Works on desktop and phone; targets that no longer exist show as 'removed'. Backfill hooks for already shipped entries from their reports/plugin.json ui blocks. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control ('open what build X changed'). Tests: a hook opens the right view and highlights the element.

origin.said: Whenever you click the shipped feature, a built plan or anything related to a UI or setting, it brings you to it. There's got to be a hook to it. Somewhere, either clicking it or a hook somewhere in its expanded row or something.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Console approval pop-up: Approve / Deny act in place, never open new browser windows or tabs (find what opens them and stop it)
axHub policy: veto only for calls that write to the VPS or switch Claude accounts; console planner/orchestrator/plan writes and other non-VPS writes run as allow (audited)
Update shared rules + decisions.md, tests

before.title: Owner-only settings: Brett's admin console login counts as owner
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> won't let me set it. It says no way enabled by owner only. Only Brett changes it. With his own click in the console. ... I can't click it.

Problem: Settings → Plugins → Claude refuses owner-only switches (No wait) for Brett's signed-in admin console session. Fix the owner check so Brett's own login is recognised as owner. Queue behind the account/badge build (one build at a time).

before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

steps.text: Switching the active account actually signs the VPS Claude login in to it (live login matches active), banner clock badge goes live
Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Console approval pop-up: Approve / Deny act in place, never open new browser windows or tabs (find what opens them and stop it)
axHub policy: veto only for calls that write to the VPS or switch Claude accounts; console planner/orchestrator/plan writes and other non-VPS writes run as allow (audited)
Update shared rules + decisions.md, tests
