Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: AmberX APK + AXHub web: open any website (follow-up to axHub #114, PR #39)
before.detail: axHub now sends other sites as browser.open {url, browser, external:true} to capability open-any-url@1. Until the APK advertises it, the hub answers install the new AmberX APK, so www.hostinger.com still will not open.

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: We need a plugin that will let AmberX open up any website I tell her to.

steps.text: amberx-droid: OpenUrlRules accepts external:true (http or https, any host and port; still no other scheme, no user info; own-site check unchanged otherwise), default browser unless asked; AxppLink advertises open-any-url@1; notification wording for other sites; OpenUrlRulesTest. Note java.net.URI is stricter than the hub URL parser.
axhub-web: screen for the open_url setting (own / allowlist / any, allowlist editing) on /auth/api/amberx/open-url, shown when session can.openUrlSettings.

before.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
before.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett (Nov 9): "needs a way to go through all the pending builds and the build queue and search for steps that are gonna break existing work or conflict with it, or it's already done, or it doesn't need it anymore." Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

before.detail: Today every orchestrator brief says 'read only the files listed' but lists no files. Also trim the brief: Brett's words once (not twice), steps, files, how to tick steps; drop boilerplate that doesn't apply to the step (look/token rules only for UI steps). before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.

Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running

axHub policy: veto only for calls that write to the VPS or switch Claude accounts; console planner/orchestrator/plan writes and other non-VPS writes run as allow (audited)

before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
before.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett (Nov 9): "needs a way to go through all the pending builds and the build queue and search for steps that are gonna break existing work or conflict with it, or it's already done, or it doesn't need it anymore." Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

steps.text: Switching the active account actually signs the VPS Claude login in to it (live login matches active), banner clock badge goes live
Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Console approval pop-up: Approve / Deny act in place, never open new browser windows or tabs (find what opens them and stop it)
axHub policy: veto only for calls that write to the VPS or switch Claude accounts; console planner/orchestrator/plan writes and other non-VPS writes run as allow (audited)

before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: grindr-ai-wingman
before.detail: AI wingman for Brett's own Grindr account, using credentials he saves in axHub. 1) Browse and shortlist: filter profiles on what people write in their profiles (stats, what they're into, looking for), favor serious, active, complete profiles, skip time-wasters; send Brett the shortlist. No copying or storing other people's photos. 2) Honest outreach: first message always says it's Brett's AI assistant/friend reaching out for him; it never claims to be human or to be Brett, never invents facts about Brett, and stays truthful. If someone isn't interested or asks it to stop, it stops and never messages them again. Light rate limit. When someone replies with interest, hand the chat to Brett. Warn Brett in the UI that Grindr may ban accounts it detects as automated. Voice + API/MCP/CLI parity. Orchestrator assigns models.

before.title: Briefs list the existing files each step needs
before.detail: Today every orchestrator brief says 'read only the files listed' but lists no files. When the orchestrator splits a build into steps, it looks up the existing files each step will need (plugin folders, plugin.json, server/web entry points, schemas, the CLI/engine files it extends) from the plugin/UI registry, the Shipped features ledger and a quick grep, and writes them into the brief per step as 'Start with these files'. New files are not listed. Keep the list short (the files that matter, not whole folders). Also trim the brief: Brett's words once (not twice), steps, files, how to tick steps; drop boilerplate that doesn't apply to the step (look/token rules only for UI steps). Tests: brief template lists files per step; a UI step gets the look rules, a non-UI step doesn't; Brett's words appear once.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

origin.said: Better to have it list the files that it already knows it's gonna need, and then it can read those files and determine what to do. It will help it determine what to do.

after.title: Skins are a complete rework: look + layout + behavior, and professional skins
after.detail: After skins-finish lands (skin@1 + skin-coverage@1 for every asset type). Today a skin covers look only; layout and behavior live in design packs. Change: a skin is the complete rework of an app. Extend skin@1 (contract, Fable) to carry everything a design pack does: look (colors, grid and hover/selection colors, typography sizes, spacing/density, radius, borders, shadows, icons, motion), layout (nav placement, app menu, toolbars, banners, panel arrangement, grid density) and behavior (how menus open/slide/collapse, context menu style, hover/press feedback, transitions, overflow rules) for every registry asset type: nav menu, app menu, context menu, grids, dialogs, windows, bars, widgets, text. Design packs fold into skins (migrate, keep a compatibility alias). Applying a skin swaps all of it at once and resets rolled assets (UI Roller rule). CI: every asset type has skin coverage for look, layout and behavior. Then design at least 5 complete professional skins (clean enterprise, dark pro, compact data, modern SaaS, plus one more), applied to the real console, AmberX and Molly; post each to UI Review with desktop and phone shots; the pick becomes the default. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests; report.

origin.said: I want the skins to be everything. I want a skin to be a complete rework. Everything. The skins are gonna rewrite the navigation menu, the app menu, the context menu, all the colors in the grids, the hover colors, the text sizes. All the behavior, everything. I need the entire UI reworked to look professional.

before.title: skins-asset-types
before.detail: Upgrade skins to style every registry asset type (widgets, icon packs, composites, embeds, text blocks), scoped inheritance, registry-driven coverage + CI check. Brief: /root/axf-builds/skins-asset-types/.brief.md. Was queued directly; orchestrator to assign models.

notes.text: Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.said: What about skins? How's skins doing? Is skins gonna um, be upgraded since we've we've made um so many more asset types? ... Added into skins.

addenda.said: Upgrade the skins system so it styles EVERY asset type now in the registry, not just the original kinds. Cover the new types: embeddable widget, icon pack, composite assets (button = box + text, nav = container + items), data set bar (search/filter/sort), embed, and every element down to text blocks/labels. Skins apply at any scope: global/app/UI/plugin, with child-overrides-parent inheritance (same model as design/icon packs). A skin is a design pack; it MAY reference an icon pack but doesn't have to. Pull the full asset-type list from the registry dynamically so new types are covered automatically going forward (no hardcoded list); add a CI check that fails if a registered asset type has no skin coverage. Voice + API/MCP/CLI parity. Submit at least 3 UI options to UI Review first.

steps.text: skin-coverage@1 engine: coverage of every registry type (slot / parts / reference / bundle / none) derived from asset-types.json, scope chain global → app → UI → plugin (child overrides parent), fixtures; registry declarations for the few types with no look
skin@1 extension: parts, iconPack, per-scope skins in app-look@1 + composeLook per scope; validators (TS + build engine), schemas, gen-fixtures
CI: check-skin-coverage fails on a registered type with no skin coverage; android.yml; rebake; typecheck; checks
Customize targets for every drawn type (widgets, badge, label, text): composite parts box / text / icon / items
Runtime + React: scope-aware skins on plugin roots and view roots, parts sheet, icon pack setting
Settings → Appearance: scope picker, Follow global switch, coverage list; 3 UI options to UI Review
CLI / API / MCP / voice parity: skins.mjs scopes + coverage, theme-manager routes, console actions
Docs, PORTING, rules, report, THREADS, PR into the merge queue; close skins s9–s11

after.title: Skins are a complete rework: look + layout + behavior, and professional skins
after.detail: After skins-finish lands (skin@1 + skin-coverage@1 for every asset type). Today a skin covers look only; layout and behavior live in design packs. Change: a skin is the complete rework of an app. Extend skin@1 (contract, Fable) to carry everything a design pack does: look (colors, grid and hover/selection colors, typography sizes, spacing/density, radius, borders, shadows, icons, motion), layout (nav placement, app menu, toolbars, banners, panel arrangement, grid density) and behavior (how menus open/slide/collapse, context menu style, hover/press feedback, transitions, overflow rules) for every registry asset type: nav menu, app menu, context menu, grids, dialogs, windows, bars, widgets, text. Design packs fold into skins (migrate, keep a compatibility alias). Applying a skin swaps all of it at once and resets rolled assets (UI Roller rule). CI: every asset type has skin coverage for look, layout and behavior. Then design at least 5 complete professional skins (clean enterprise, dark pro, compact data, modern SaaS, plus one more), applied to the real console, AmberX and Molly; post each to UI Review with desktop and phone shots; the pick becomes the default. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests; report.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.

Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running

before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).

"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."

Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: Briefs list the existing files each step needs
before.detail: Today every orchestrator brief says 'read only the files listed' but lists no files. When the orchestrator splits a build into steps, it looks up the existing files each step will need (plugin folders, plugin.json, server/web entry points, schemas, the CLI/engine files it extends) from the plugin/UI registry, the Shipped features ledger and a quick grep, and writes them into the brief per step as 'Start with these files'. New files are not listed. Keep the list short (the files that matter, not whole folders). Also trim the brief: Brett's words once (not twice), steps, files, how to tick steps; drop boilerplate that doesn't apply to the step (look/token rules only for UI steps). Tests: brief template lists files per step; a UI step gets the look rules, a non-UI step doesn't; Brett's words appear once.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

origin.said: Better to have it list the files that it already knows it's gonna need, and then it can read those files and determine what to do. It will help it determine what to do.

before.title: Skins are a complete rework: look + layout + behavior, and professional skins
before.detail: After skins-finish lands (skin@1 + skin-coverage@1 for every asset type). Today a skin covers look only; layout and behavior live in design packs. Change: a skin is the complete rework of an app. Extend skin@1 (contract, Fable) to carry everything a design pack does: look (colors, grid and hover/selection colors, typography sizes, spacing/density, radius, borders, shadows, icons, motion), layout (nav placement, app menu, toolbars, banners, panel arrangement, grid density) and behavior (how menus open/slide/collapse, context menu style, hover/press feedback, transitions, overflow rules) for every registry asset type: nav menu, app menu, context menu, grids, dialogs, windows, bars, widgets, text. Design packs fold into skins (migrate, keep a compatibility alias). Applying a skin swaps all of it at once and resets rolled assets (UI Roller rule). CI: every asset type has skin coverage for look, layout and behavior. Then design at least 5 complete professional skins (clean enterprise, dark pro, compact data, modern SaaS, plus one more), applied to the real console, AmberX and Molly; post each to UI Review with desktop and phone shots; the pick becomes the default. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests; report.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

I need the entire UI reworked to look professional.

after.title: Reserve build IDs at once: add returns the ID with the veto countdown
after.detail: Today pending_change add (and control_add on planner.builds/plans) is held on the 90 s veto countdown and the orchestrator only assigns the build ID when it runs, so callers (Claude sessions) must guess the ID from the title to add notes. Fix: the orchestrator (ID registry) reserves the ID the moment the call arrives, before the hold, and returns it in the held result (e.g. reservedId). Notes, sub prompts and status calls on a reserved ID queue up and apply in order once the add runs; if Brett denies the add, the reservation and anything queued on it are dropped. IDs never collide (registry check). Same for plan_park and plan_add. Tests: add returns the id while held; a note on the reserved id lands after the add; deny drops both.

origin.said: Why do you have to guess its ID? Why can't you get it? ... Yeah, of course.

Fix: the orchestrator (ID registry) reserves the ID the moment the call arrives, before the hold, and returns it in the held result (e.g. reservedId). Notes, sub prompts and status calls on a reserved ID queue up and apply in order once the add runs; if Brett denies the add, the reservation and anything queued on it are dropped. IDs never collide (registry check). Same for plan_park and plan_add. Tests: add returns the id while held; a note on the reserved id lands after the add; deny drops both.

origin.said: Why do you have to guess its ID? Why can't you get it? ... Yeah, of course.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch

Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Console approval pop-up: Approve / Deny act in place, never open new browser windows or tabs (find what opens them and stop it)
axHub policy: veto only for calls that write to the VPS or switch Claude accounts; console planner/orchestrator/plan writes and other non-VPS writes run as allow (audited)
Update shared rules + decisions.md, tests

before.title: Owner-only settings: Brett's admin console login counts as owner
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> won't let me set it. It says no way enabled by owner only. Only Brett changes it. With his own click in the console. ... I can't click it.
> I'm logged in as admin.

Problem: Settings → Plugins → Claude refuses owner-only switches (No wait) for Brett's signed-in admin console session. Fix the owner check so Brett's own login is recognised as owner. Queue behind the account/badge build (one build at a time).

before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).

"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.

before.title: Reserve build IDs at once: add returns the ID with the veto countdown
before.detail: Today pending_change add (and control_add on planner.builds/plans) is held on the 90 s veto countdown and the orchestrator only assigns the build ID when it runs, so callers (Claude sessions) must guess the ID from the title to add notes. Fix: the orchestrator (ID registry) reserves the ID the moment the call arrives, before the hold, and returns it in the held result (e.g. reservedId). Notes, sub prompts and status calls on a reserved ID queue up and apply in order once the add runs; if Brett denies the add, the reservation and anything queued on it are dropped. IDs never collide (registry check). Same for plan_park and plan_add. Tests: add returns the id while held; a note on the reserved id lands after the add; deny drops both.

before.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
before.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.

Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

Correction (Brett): the Sweep does NOT run automatically on every land. It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). Flags found at dispatch hold the build for Brett instead of launching.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.

# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).

"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."

before.title: Permissions control panel: every axHub tool's policy in one place
before.detail: Repo: axHub (policy store) + console/axhub-web screen. One Permissions panel listing every connected service and every tool (vps.build_start, vps.run, axf-console.*, github, hostinger, amberx...) with its policy (allow / veto countdown / confirm / deny), countdown length, who may call it (Brett's sessions, Claude sessions, headless builds, agents), and passes. Brett changes a policy with a dropdown; bulk change per service or by filter (destructive, writes, reads). Tree grouped by service > category, search, filters, live type-ahead. Every change logged with history and undo. Claude sessions and builds can read policies but never change them (owner-only, enforced on the hub, not just the UI). First change: set vps.build_start to deny so only the orchestrator launches builds. Full API (read for all, write owner-only), voice for Brett. 3 layout options to UI Review.

origin.said: I need a control panel for all those settings, those permission settings.

notes.text: Brett: "Can I make it so that employees like Molly or Amber or Moses can use it, and then I assign one of the employees to the orchestrator so the orchestrator can say run it, change it?" Permissions are granted per employee (agent from the one roster: Molly, Amber, Moses, Brownie, etc.), not just per session type. Brett assigns an employee to the orchestrator; the orchestrator acts with that employee's permissions. Brett can grant an employee permission to change policies, but only within a ceiling Brett sets: an employee can never raise its own or another's permissions above the ceiling, never touch owner-only settings or the ceiling itself, every change it makes is logged with the employee's name and sends Brett a notification, and Brett can revoke instantly. Panel shows per-employee view and per-tool view.

origin.brief:
# Build: plan-studio-receives-a-valid-shipped-feature-man

## Brett said (verbatim)
> Make sure it creates the plant studio, make sure it gets all the, the correct information, the fields of the manifest are sent to the plant studio. So the plant studio's gotta receive a manifest too. It has to be valid.

## What to build
Continue build "Plan Studio receives a valid shipped-feature manifest" (plan-studio-receives-a-valid-shipped-feature-man) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"Make sure it creates the plant studio, make sure it gets all the, the correct information, the fields of the manifest are sent to the plant studio. So the plant studio's gotta receive a manifest too. It has to be valid."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (1 left, ~30 min):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Follow-up to build shipped-manifest-api (branch claude/shipped-manifest-api, shipped-manifest@1). When the orchestrator sends a shipped-feature manifest to the Shipped Features ledger, it also sends the same manifest to Plan Studio: create (or update) the build's Plan Studio plan with every manifest field (build id/title, Brett's verbatim prompt highlighted, full brief, models/accounts, steps with estimates and actual times, branch, PR, landed commit, files changed, tests, UI Review item, cost/tokens, report path, open items). Plan Studio validates it against the shipped-manifest@1 schema and rejects or flags an invalid one (shown in the plan and the terminal). Shared schema module, no copy. Backfill tonight's landed builds. Full API control (MCP/CLI/deep link/voice). Tests: valid manifest creates a matching plan, invalid one is refused with the reason; plans.mjs check-builds stays green.
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step plan-studio-receives-a-valid-shipped-feature-man <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link plan-studio-receives-a-valid-shipped-feature-man --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account account-3 for the Fable phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step plan-studio-receives-a-valid-shipped-feature-man <stepId> done). When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note plan-studio-receives-a-valid-shipped-feature-man "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

before.detail: Repo: axHub (policy store) + console/axhub-web screen. One Permissions panel listing every connected service and every tool (vps.build_start, vps.run, axf-console.*, github, hostinger, amberx...) with its policy (allow / veto countdown / confirm / deny), countdown length, who may call it (Brett's sessions, Claude sessions, headless builds, agents), and passes. First change: set vps.build_start to deny so only the orchestrator launches builds. Full API (read for all, write owner-only), voice for Brett. 3 layout options to UI Review.

notes.text: Brett: "Can I make it so that employees like Molly or Amber or Moses can use it, and then I assign one of the employees to the orchestrator so the orchestrator can say run it, change it?" Permissions are granted per employee (agent from the one roster: Molly, Amber, Moses, Brownie, etc.), not just per session type. Brett assigns an employee to the orchestrator; the orchestrator acts with that employee's permissions. Brett can grant an employee permission to change policies, but only within a ceiling Brett sets: an employee can never raise its own or another's permissions above the ceiling, never touch owner-only settings or the ceiling itself, every change it makes is logged with the employee's name and sends Brett a notification, and Brett can revoke instantly. Panel shows per-employee view and per-tool view.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

steps.text: Switching the active account actually signs the VPS Claude login in to it (live login matches active), banner clock badge goes live
Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

origin.said: "The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs." Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."
origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: Permissions control panel: every axHub tool's policy in one place
before.detail: Repo: axHub (policy store) + console/axhub-web screen. One Permissions panel listing every connected service and every tool (vps.build_start, vps.run, axf-console.*, github, hostinger, amberx...) with its policy (allow / veto countdown / confirm / deny), countdown length, who may call it (Brett's sessions, Claude sessions, headless builds, agents), and passes. Brett changes a policy with a dropdown; bulk change per service or by filter (destructive, writes, reads). Tree grouped by service > category, search, filters, live type-ahead. Every change logged with history and undo. Claude sessions and builds can read policies but never change them (owner-only, enforced on the hub, not just the UI). First change: set vps.build_start to deny so only the orchestrator launches builds. Full API (read for all, write owner-only), voice for Brett. 3 layout options to UI Review.

notes.text: Brett: "Can I make it so that employees like Molly or Amber or Moses can use it, and then I assign one of the employees to the orchestrator so the orchestrator can say run it, change it?" Permissions are granted per employee (agent from the one roster: Molly, Amber, Moses, Brownie, etc.), not just per session type. Brett assigns an employee to the orchestrator; the orchestrator acts with that employee's permissions. Brett can grant an employee permission to change policies, but only within a ceiling Brett sets: an employee can never raise its own or another's permissions above the ceiling, never touch owner-only settings or the ceiling itself, every change it makes is logged with the employee's name and sends Brett a notification, and Brett can revoke instantly. Panel shows per-employee view and per-tool view.
