before.title: Demonstration Designer plugin (new, standalone)
before.detail: New standalone console plugin 'Demonstration Designer' (own nav entry), replacing the disabled glossary-index one. Brett found the old one unusable, so make it simple and obvious. Pick any screen, plugin or UI element from the live registry, then build a demo: steps (open screen, highlight, click/type action, wait), narration text + voice, captions, timing. Record a demo by doing it, edit it on a timeline, preview, play it live on the console or a sandboxed preview, export as video. Demos are saved assets, reusable and chainable into longer tours. Harvest useful code from the disabled glossary-index plugin (demos.mjs, walkthrough engine) instead of starting from zero. RULE: every UI action and setting has API + voice + MCP/CLI control, and a deep link opens it. Settings in categorized collapsible sections; 3 UI options to UI Review; tests; report.

notes.text: PURPOSE (Brett): it's for PITCHING the product. Keep it dead simple. Main flow = three picks: (1) plugin or topic, (2) length in minutes, (3) narrator voice; then ONE Generate button. Generate writes a pitch script (hook up front, benefits not specs, closing call to action), picks the best screens, and plays a polished demo on real data: highlights, smooth zooms/pans, captions, background music, logo intro/outro. After: optional script tweak, preview, export video (MP4) or share link. Advanced editing (timeline, record-by-doing) stays tucked behind an Advanced section, never in the main flow.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.
Queued by cli.

Brett: "Why doesn't the exported video have the narrator's voice? AmberX can screen record it." Phase 1 export uses browser speech, which Chrome doesn't route into tab capture, so videos have captions and music but no voice. Fix: add an export option 'Record on AmberX': the demo plays on Brett's phone and AmberX records it with the narration audio (reuse AmberX's Audio Output Recorder, extend it to screen + app audio), then uploads the video back to the demo asset. Also a default export path that doesn't need the phone: generate the narration as real audio (a TTS voice) and mix it into the exported MP4. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Running headless builds pick up the active account on switch
Failover: on limit/auth death, switch to the next live account by itself and resume
Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew
Tests + banner item when no account is left

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

steps.text: Console approval pop-up: Approve / Deny act in place, never open new browser windows or tabs (find what opens them and stop it)
axHub policy: veto only for calls that write to the VPS or switch Claude accounts; console planner/orchestrator/plan writes and other non-VPS writes run as allow (audited)
Update shared rules + decisions.md, tests

before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: Briefs list the existing files each step needs
before.detail: Today every orchestrator brief says 'read only the files listed' but lists no files. When the orchestrator splits a build into steps, it looks up the existing files each step will need (plugin folders, plugin.json, server/web entry points, schemas, the CLI/engine files it extends) from the plugin/UI registry, the Shipped features ledger and a quick grep, and writes them into the brief per step as 'Start with these files'. New files are not listed. Keep the list short (the files that matter, not whole folders). Also trim the brief: Brett's words once (not twice), steps, files, how to tick steps; drop boilerplate that doesn't apply to the step (look/token rules only for UI steps). Tests: brief template lists files per step; a UI step gets the look rules, a non-UI step doesn't; Brett's words appear once.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

origin.said: Better to have it list the files that it already knows it's gonna need, and then it can read those files and determine what to do. It will help it determine what to do.

after.title: Session transcripts API: search what was said, find which session
after.detail: Builds on ui-review-notify-session-audio (landed Nov 7): sessions are recorded by AmberX's Audio Output Recorder (output-recorder plugin) and transcribed by the faster-whisper worker, transcripts saved on the hub, readable in the recorder page. Today output-recorder's plugin.json declares no transcript commands, so nothing outside the page can read them. Add full API (plugin-commands@1, so MCP/axHub, REST, CLI, voice come for free): list sessions with transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title); read one transcript (whole or a time range, with timestamps); search across all transcripts (words or phrase, date range, fuzzy), returning the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context, and a deep link that opens the recorder page at that moment (and plays the audio there). Also a 'find the session where we talked about X' command that ranks sessions by match. Reachable from Claude chat/voice sessions through axHub so Claude or Gizmo can answer 'which session did we talk about this'. Read-only; respects the recorder's settings. Tests; report.

origin.said: I want the API to be able to access the transcript so I can tell you or I can tell Gizmo, you know, what session was it that we talked about this or that.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).

"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."

before.title: Session transcripts API: search what was said, find which session
before.detail: Builds on ui-review-notify-session-audio (landed Nov 7): sessions are recorded by AmberX's Audio Output Recorder (output-recorder plugin) and transcribed by the faster-whisper worker, transcripts saved on the hub, readable in the recorder page. Today output-recorder's plugin.json declares no transcript commands, so nothing outside the page can read them. Add full API (plugin-commands@1, so MCP/axHub, REST, CLI, voice come for free): list sessions with transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title); read one transcript (whole or a time range, with timestamps); search across all transcripts (words or phrase, date range, fuzzy), returning the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context, and a deep link that opens the recorder page at that moment (and plays the audio there). Also a 'find the session where we talked about X' command that ranks sessions by match. Reachable from Claude chat/voice sessions through axHub so Claude or Gizmo can answer 'which session did we talk about this'. Read-only; respects the recorder's settings. Tests; report.

origin.said: I want the API to be able to access the transcript so I can tell you or I can tell Gizmo, you know, what session was it that we talked about this or that.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

before.title: Briefs list the existing files each step needs
before.detail: Today every orchestrator brief says 'read only the files listed' but lists no files. When the orchestrator splits a build into steps, it looks up the existing files each step will need (plugin folders, plugin.json, server/web entry points, schemas, the CLI/engine files it extends) from the plugin/UI registry, the Shipped features ledger and a quick grep, and writes them into the brief per step as 'Start with these files'. New files are not listed. Keep the list short (the files that matter, not whole folders). Also trim the brief: Brett's words once (not twice), steps, files, how to tick steps; drop boilerplate that doesn't apply to the step (look/token rules only for UI steps). Tests: brief template lists files per step; a UI step gets the look rules, a non-UI step doesn't; Brett's words appear once.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

origin.said: Better to have it list the files that it already knows it's gonna need, and then it can read those files and determine what to do. It will help it determine what to do.

before.title: Session transcripts API: search what was said, find which session
before.detail: Builds on ui-review-notify-session-audio (landed Nov 7): sessions are recorded by AmberX's Audio Output Recorder (output-recorder plugin) and transcribed by the faster-whisper worker, transcripts saved on the hub, readable in the recorder page. Today output-recorder's plugin.json declares no transcript commands, so nothing outside the page can read them. Add full API (plugin-commands@1, so MCP/axHub, REST, CLI, voice come for free): list sessions with transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title); read one transcript (whole or a time range, with timestamps); search across all transcripts (words or phrase, date range, fuzzy), returning the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context, and a deep link that opens the recorder page at that moment (and plays the audio there). Also a 'find the session where we talked about X' command that ranks sessions by match. Reachable from Claude chat/voice sessions through axHub so Claude or Gizmo can answer 'which session did we talk about this'. Read-only; respects the recorder's settings. Tests; report.

notes.text: Brett: "I can find that internally without AI, right?" Yes: all search is plain code with zero tokens (full-text index over the transcripts, phrase + fuzzy + date filters). Add a search box with live type-ahead results on the recorder page and in the console's Search everything, so Brett can find a session himself without any AI. Claude/Gizmo only call the same plain search through the API.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

origin.said: I want the API to be able to access the transcript so I can tell you or I can tell Gizmo, you know, what session was it that we talked about this or that.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running

before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: Session transcripts API: search what was said, find which session
before.detail: Builds on ui-review-notify-session-audio (landed Nov 7): sessions are recorded by AmberX's Audio Output Recorder (output-recorder plugin) and transcribed by the faster-whisper worker, transcripts saved on the hub, readable in the recorder page. Today output-recorder's plugin.json declares no transcript commands, so nothing outside the page can read them. Add full API (plugin-commands@1, so MCP/axHub, REST, CLI, voice come for free): list sessions with transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title); read one transcript (whole or a time range, with timestamps); search across all transcripts (words or phrase, date range, fuzzy), returning the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context, and a deep link that opens the recorder page at that moment (and plays the audio there). Also a 'find the session where we talked about X' command that ranks sessions by match. Reachable from Claude chat/voice sessions through axHub so Claude or Gizmo can answer 'which session did we talk about this'. Read-only; respects the recorder's settings. Tests; report.

notes.text: Brett: "I can find that internally without AI, right?" Yes: all search is plain code with zero tokens (full-text index over the transcripts, phrase + fuzzy + date filters). Add a search box with live type-ahead results on the recorder page and in the console's Search everything, so Brett can find a session himself without any AI. Claude/Gizmo only call the same plain search through the API.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: results pop up in a scrolling window. As Brett types in Search everything (or the recorder page), matching transcript snippets pop up live in a scrolling results window: each hit shows the session (date, title), timestamp and a few lines around the match with the words highlighted; infinite scroll, grouped by session, newest first with a sort switch. Tapping a hit opens the recorder at that moment and plays the audio. Plain search also drops filler phrases like 'find the session where', 'when we talked about' so a whole sentence still works, zero tokens.

origin.said: I want the API to be able to access the transcript so I can tell you or I can tell Gizmo, you know, what session was it that we talked about this or that.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). Not ticked: no live policy changed; it needs that build's Fable step s4 (axHub policy API) and Brett's Apply click. s1 pop-up windows and s3 rules are untouched.
s1 / s4-3 covered by PR 375 (claude/approvals-in-place-r2): Approve and Deny act in place, nothing opens a window. The policy and rules steps are untouched.

Reconciler: paused: no live session or process runs it (worktree kept); was running

before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).
5. Shared registry (schema + store + read/write API with change events) used by both the Claude plugin and Claude MD Studio.
6. Shared controls in both plugins: CLAUDE.md chain view in load order with size and tokens; per-file include/exclude and always / on demand / never, reorder, edit, preview; per-build and per-step overrides; session mode, handoff size, model rules; output caps, file scoping, token budget per step with warn/stop; live token cost preview; presets lean/normal/full, reset, history.
7. API, CLI and MCP for the registry.
8. Verify savings with the token log on a test build.

Stay out of apps/console-web/plugins/ai-keys and the Gizmo companion plugin (other builds). Don't load the full CLAUDE.md chain. Tick steps as they finish. PR, do not land.

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: grindr-ai-wingman
before.detail: AI wingman for Brett's own Grindr account, using credentials he saves in axHub. 1) Browse and shortlist: filter profiles on what people write in their profiles (stats, what they're into, looking for), favor serious, active, complete profiles, skip time-wasters; send Brett the shortlist. No copying or storing other people's photos. 2) Honest outreach: first message always says it's Brett's AI assistant/friend reaching out for him; it never claims to be human or to be Brett, never invents facts about Brett, and stays truthful. Warn Brett in the UI that Grindr may ban accounts it detects as automated. Voice + API/MCP/CLI parity. Orchestrator assigns models.

before.title: Briefs list the existing files each step needs
before.detail: Today every orchestrator brief says 'read only the files listed' but lists no files. New files are not listed. Keep the list short (the files that matter, not whole folders). Also trim the brief: Brett's words once (not twice), steps, files, how to tick steps; drop boilerplate that doesn't apply to the step (look/token rules only for UI steps). Tests: brief template lists files per step; a UI step gets the look rules, a non-UI step doesn't; Brett's words appear once.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

origin.said: Better to have it list the files that it already knows it's gonna need, and then it can read those files and determine what to do. It will help it determine what to do.

before.title: Session transcripts API: search what was said, find which session
before.detail: Builds on ui-review-notify-session-audio (landed Nov 7): sessions are recorded by AmberX's Audio Output Recorder (output-recorder plugin) and transcribed by the faster-whisper worker, transcripts saved on the hub, readable in the recorder page. Today output-recorder's plugin.json declares no transcript commands, so nothing outside the page can read them. Add full API (plugin-commands@1, so MCP/axHub, REST, CLI, voice come for free): list sessions with transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title); read one transcript (whole or a time range, with timestamps); search across all transcripts (words or phrase, date range, fuzzy), returning the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context, and a deep link that opens the recorder page at that moment (and plays the audio there). Also a 'find the session where we talked about X' command that ranks sessions by match. Reachable from Claude chat/voice sessions through axHub so Claude or Gizmo can answer 'which session did we talk about this'. Read-only; respects the recorder's settings. Tests; report.

notes.text: Brett: "I can find that internally without AI, right?" Yes: all search is plain code with zero tokens (full-text index over the transcripts, phrase + fuzzy + date filters). Add a search box with live type-ahead results on the recorder page and in the console's Search everything, so Brett can find a session himself without any AI. Claude/Gizmo only call the same plain search through the API.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: results pop up in a scrolling window. As Brett types in Search everything (or the recorder page), matching transcript snippets pop up live in a scrolling results window: each hit shows the session (date, title), timestamp and a few lines around the match with the words highlighted; infinite scroll, grouped by session, newest first with a sort switch. Tapping a hit opens the recorder at that moment and plays the audio. Plain search also drops filler phrases like 'find the session where', 'when we talked about' so a whole sentence still works, zero tokens.

Brett: "With the keywords in focus." In the scrolling results window each snippet is centered on the matched keywords, highlighted. Opening a hit scrolls the transcript so the keyword is centered on screen, highlighted and focused, with next/previous match buttons inside that session.

origin.said: I want the API to be able to access the transcript so I can tell you or I can tell Gizmo, you know, what session was it that we talked about this or that.

before.title: Running builds follow the active Claude account, fail over when it dies
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> the running builds need to run on whatever account's connected. If, if the account dies, they need to switch over.
> Every time you log in with a refresh token, you need to update the refresh token.
> why doesn't it switch over? It needs to switch over on its own.

Context: claude_accounts_use to account-2 succeeded and marked it active, but the live VPS login stayed gizmox1111 (loginChanged: true) and the banner clock badge stayed gray. Reverses part of build-own-login (#357). Related: ai-keys-console-store (#358), console-account-picker. Check overlap first.

notes.text: The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
The 'Save the rotated refresh token' steps are built by first-refresh-token-saved-every-time-it-s-used-v (PR #359): tick them once it merges, don't rebuild them.
Overlap (multi-account-headless-workers): failover is built for worker accounts. Following the active account is unchanged, and any switch must skip workers.
Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

Steps 3-5 (failover on limit/auth death, save rotated token back, banner/alert when no account is left) are built in account-failover-notify (branch claude/account-failover-notify). Steps 1-2 (switching the active account re-signs the VPS login; running builds follow the switch) remain.

Overlap: account-health-failover (PR #394) adds the shared account-status@1 store and capability axf.account-status@1 (able(name, model)): use it to pick the account to switch to instead of a new check.

Save the rotated refresh token back after every login/renew

before.title: Approvals: no window spam on Approve; veto only for VPS writes and account switches
before.detail:
## Brett said (verbatim)
Source: voice · At: 2026-11-06
> when I click approve and the consoles pop up, I don't want it to launch a window of access. It's opening a thousand fucking windows. And also you only need to send the veto rules that ask for approval or deny if you are actually writing something to the VPS or if you are switching accounts.
> All right, go ahead, build that shit.

Notes: touches Follow Amber approval pop-up (console) and axHub tool policies (veto vs allow). Changing which calls are veto is a policy change in axHub and the shared rule 'It's a veto system'; update rules + decisions.md to match.

notes.text: Overlap with claude-settings-tabs-veto (PR 371): its Approvals & veto tab is the tool for s2 / s5-4 (default plan: hold only VPS writes and account switches). before.title: Headless session efficiency + shared chain control
before.detail: Follow-on to headless-progress-file-lean-claude-md-chain. Cut headless token spend and give Brett full, meticulous control over the CLAUDE.md chain. All settings live in a shared registry that both the Claude plugin and the Claude MD Studio plugin read and write (Brett, voice, Nov 6 2026).

notes.text: Merged from build profile "current" into "all" (one profile for everything).

origin.brief:
# Build: md-chain-control (pending item headless-session-efficiency-shared-chain-control)

Brett: finish the optimization in Claude MD Studio. The token log, rules briefs and headless-skips-CLAUDE.md work is on branch claude/token-optimize (PR open, not merged): merge origin/claude/token-optimize into this branch first and build on it; don't redo any of it.

That item lists every step twice; do each once:
1. Fresh session per step with a short handoff note from the progress file.
2. Per-step model choice suggested by the orchestrator.
3. Steps list the exact files they need; sessions read only those.
4. Trim long tool output (configurable caps).

origin.brief:
# Build: claude-settings-tabs-veto

## Brett said (verbatim)
"The Claude settings interface is getting pretty big. We need to organize it. Give it multiple views, one of them being tabular. If you have it on the tab view, you can set where you want them to appear and how you want them to appear: on the left, on the right, on the top, and the bottom, whether you want the words or an icon." "The veto and the approve are gonna be their own tab in there. Break it down and put it into tabs."
Also: "You don't need to run the 90-second veto thing unless you are writing stuff to the VPS."

1. Audit Claude settings (plugin claude-settings): list every setting, group them into sensible tabs. Report the breakdown.
2. Views: classic (one page, collapsible sections) and tabbed. Tabbed uses the tab-group@1 asset: tab position left / right / top / bottom, labels as words / icons / both. Settings for the view saved per device. Claude settings stays a settings-interface asset.
3. New tab 'Approvals & veto': per axHub tool (or group) choose allow / veto / confirm, veto hold length (seconds), pass durations; reads go without a hold, only VPS writes and account switches hold by default. Writes to the axHub policy through its API (owner-only). Show the current policy table live.
4. REST/MCP/CLI for the view settings and the policy tab.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly. Overlap check with pending item approvals-no-window-spam-on-approve-veto-only-for-vps-writes-and-account-switc; tick its veto step if covered, note it.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, UI registry, badges/notifications code (other builds).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - where the veto/approval settings live
"Those settings should not be part of the Claude plugin. They can be accessed by any MCP server, the API or the CLI. They can be in Claude settings, they can be in framework settings."
- The approvals/veto policy settings are their own framework-level settings asset (settings-ui@1), owned by the framework, not the claude-settings plugin. Store: framework settings. Exposed on REST + MCP + CLI.
- Mounted in two places as the same asset: Framework settings and a tab in Claude settings. One source of truth.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - predicted options first
"Give me a bunch of options in UI Review to pick from, like ten."
- BEFORE building the UI: submit 10 predicted screenshots (ui-review-predicted) of where/how Framework settings and the Approvals & veto settings sit in the main settings interface: e.g. own top-level Framework tab; a section inside General; a left-rail group; a settings home card; a gear in the banner; icon tabs top/left/right/bottom variants; a compact phone layout; a two-pane layout. Phone + desktop each.
- Wait for Brett's pick in UI Review, then build that one. The 10 are mockups only, no code written for the losers.

before.title: grindr-ai-wingman
before.detail: AI wingman for Brett's own Grindr account, using credentials he saves in axHub. 1) Browse and shortlist: filter profiles on what people write in their profiles (stats, what they're into, looking for), favor serious, active, complete profiles, skip time-wasters; send Brett the shortlist. No copying or storing other people's photos. 2) Honest outreach: first message always says it's Brett's AI assistant/friend reaching out for him; it never claims to be human or to be Brett, never invents facts about Brett, and stays truthful. If someone isn't interested or asks it to stop, it stops and never messages them again. Light rate limit. When someone replies with interest, hand the chat to Brett. Warn Brett in the UI that Grindr may ban accounts it detects as automated. Voice + API/MCP/CLI parity. Orchestrator assigns models.

before.title: Briefs list the existing files each step needs
before.detail: Today every orchestrator brief says 'read only the files listed' but lists no files. When the orchestrator splits a build into steps, it looks up the existing files each step will need (plugin folders, plugin.json, server/web entry points, schemas, the CLI/engine files it extends) from the plugin/UI registry, the Shipped features ledger and a quick grep, and writes them into the brief per step as 'Start with these files'. New files are not listed. Keep the list short (the files that matter, not whole folders). Also trim the brief: Brett's words once (not twice), steps, files, how to tick steps; drop boilerplate that doesn't apply to the step (look/token rules only for UI steps). Tests: brief template lists files per step; a UI step gets the look rules, a non-UI step doesn't; Brett's words appear once.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

origin.said: Better to have it list the files that it already knows it's gonna need, and then it can read those files and determine what to do. It will help it determine what to do.

before.title: Demonstration Designer plugin (new, standalone)
before.detail: New standalone console plugin 'Demonstration Designer' (own nav entry), replacing the disabled glossary-index one. Brett found the old one unusable, so make it simple and obvious. Pick any screen, plugin or UI element from the live registry, then build a demo: steps (open screen, highlight, click/type action, wait), narration text + voice, captions, timing. Record a demo by doing it, edit it on a timeline, preview, play it live on the console or a sandboxed preview, export as video. Demos are saved assets, reusable and chainable into longer tours. Harvest useful code from the disabled glossary-index plugin (demos.mjs, walkthrough engine) instead of starting from zero. RULE: every UI action and setting has API + voice + MCP/CLI control, and a deep link opens it. Settings in categorized collapsible sections; 3 UI options to UI Review; tests; report.

notes.text: PURPOSE (Brett): it's for PITCHING the product. Keep it dead simple. Main flow = three picks: (1) plugin or topic, (2) length in minutes, (3) narrator voice; then ONE Generate button. Generate writes a pitch script (hook up front, benefits not specs, closing call to action), picks the best screens, and plays a polished demo on real data: highlights, smooth zooms/pans, captions, background music, logo intro/outro. After: optional script tweak, preview, export video (MP4) or share link. Advanced editing (timeline, record-by-doing) stays tucked behind an Advanced section, never in the main flow.

Phase 1 export uses browser speech, which Chrome doesn't route into tab capture, so videos have captions and music but no voice. Also a default export path that doesn't need the phone: generate the narration as real audio (a TTS voice) and mix it into the exported MP4. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.

origin.said: What about skins? How's skins doing? Is skins gonna um, be upgraded since we've we've made um so many more asset types? ... Added into skins.

addenda.said: Upgrade the skins system so it styles EVERY asset type now in the registry, not just the original kinds. Cover the new types: embeddable widget, icon pack, composite assets (button = box + text, nav = container + items), data set bar (search/filter/sort), embed, and every element down to text blocks/labels. Skins apply at any scope: global/app/UI/plugin, with child-overrides-parent inheritance (same model as design/icon packs). A skin is a design pack; it MAY reference an icon pack but doesn't have to. Pull the full asset-type list from the registry dynamically so new types are covered automatically going forward (no hardcoded list); add a CI check that fails if a registered asset type has no skin coverage. Voice + API/MCP/CLI parity. Submit at least 3 UI options to UI Review first.

Settings → Appearance: scope picker, Follow global switch, coverage list; 3 UI options to UI Review

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.

before.title: URGENT: rebuild pipeline — orchestrator IDs, splits, Pending→Queue, slot-driven headless launches
before.detail:
Rebuild the build pipeline from scratch:
1. Everything Brett asks for becomes a build sent to the orchestrator.
2. Orchestrator assigns a build ID.
3. Orchestrator uses Claude to split it into steps (<=30 min) and picks a model per step: Fable only when needed, Opus otherwise.
4. Build goes to Pending. Brett moves Pending -> Queue.
5. Orchestrator watches the VPS: connected Claude accounts, which have Fable, max parallel and free slots per account.
6. Whenever a slot opens, the orchestrator grabs the next build in the Queue and starts a headless session on it: Fable steps to an account with Fable, everything else to Opus accounts. Never launches right away, only when a slot is free.
7. Steps tick off in the progress files per existing rules; a monitor watches them and updates progress live.

notes.text: Reconciler: PR #384 merged

origin.said: You need to start the pipeline over from scratch. From now on, what I say, send a build to the orchestrator. The orchestrator is going to assign an ID. A build ID. He's going to use you to break it up into steps select a model Babel or Opus Babel when it's needed and then he's going to see how many subscriptions are connected to the VPS how many accounts are available How many, what's the max parallel for each one? after.title: URGENT: rebuild pipeline — orchestrator IDs, splits, Pending→Queue, slot-driven headless launches
after.detail:
Rebuild the build pipeline from scratch:
1. Everything Brett asks for becomes a build sent to the orchestrator.
2. Orchestrator assigns a build ID.
3. Orchestrator uses Claude to split it into steps (<=30 min) and picks a model per step: Fable only when needed, Opus otherwise.

7. Steps tick off in the progress files per existing rules; a monitor watches them and updates progress live.

before.title: Slot-aware plan optimizer (pre-launch)
before.detail: Before the orchestrator launches a plan from the queue, it checks how many parallel sessions are enabled and how many slots are open, then optimizes/refactors the plan to use all available slots: build a dependency graph of the steps, group independent steps into parallel tracks (one per free slot), keep dependent steps in order, and give each track its own brief. Re-check slots at launch time; if slots change, re-balance.

steps.text: Read enabled parallel sessions and currently open slots at launch time
Late account binding: no account or session assigned in pending/queue; when the plan's turn comes up, count free slots on every Claude account and assign tracks across all accounts to fill every slot
Step dependency graph for a plan (which steps can run independently)
File ownership: each parallel track owns its own files; steps only run in parallel when their files don't overlap; lock shared files (configs) so sessions don't step on each other
Optimizer: split independent steps into N parallel tracks to fill free slots
Generate a separate brief per track; merge/progress markers per track
Rebalance when slots open or close mid-build + end-to-end test

Model-aware slots: when scanning accounts/slots, also read which models each account has available (Fable limit hit or not); Fable steps only go to accounts with Fable available; if no Fable anywhere, only Opus runs

One-time cleanup of current ghost 'running' builds + reaper log + end-to-end test

origin.said: Brief (headless launch, no verbatim block): Account failover + phone alerts + one home per login. 1. Automatic failover: when a build fails on an account for auth (expired/unrefreshable login) or usage limit, immediately mark that account out and relaunch the same build on the next available account (workers, then the interactive account; API accounts only per routing rules). No build should die and stay dead because of one account. Today three builds died in 1 s each on account-1 (OAuth expired) and nothing retried. 2. Phone notification (AmberX) on every such problem: which account, what failed (expired login / limit / no credits), which build moved where, and what Brett needs to do (e.g. sign account-1 in). 3. One home per login: each account's credentials live in exactly ONE store; every token refresh from any build, console or session writes back to that same place. No duplicate copies that can spend a refresh token and leave others dead. Audit claude-login.mjs / claude-token-save.mjs / claude-headless.sh and the console AI keys store for duplicates; find why account-1's refresh failed (spent by another copy vs idle expiry) and report it. 4. Status in the console Claude accounts screen: out/why/until, last refresh time per login.

before.title: Orchestrator checks Shipped features before splitting any job
before.detail: When the orchestrator receives a job and splits it into steps, it first checks the Shipped features ledger (which must hold every feature the orchestrator has ever built). It must: not build anything twice; not break or redo anything already done; and if a step would conflict with or change something already built, notify Brett (AmberX notification) and wait before going on. Make the Shipped features ledger complete (backfill every landed build) and keep it updated on every land. Also standing rule: ONLY the orchestrator launches builds, picks model and account, owns pending/queue and monitors status; voice/chat sessions only hand it requests.

notes.text: Conflict flow (Brett): a conflicting step is moved to a special Conflicts section and removed from the build; the other steps still build. Brett gets an AmberX notification-panel item that explains the conflict and offers suggested resolutions; he taps a suggestion or types a prompt, which goes to the orchestrator, and the orchestrator makes a new build from it. Then test it: Brett will send a 3-4 step build that deliberately overlaps existing shipped features to confirm the orchestrator catches it.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett (Nov 9): "needs a way to go through all the pending builds and the build queue and search for steps that are gonna break existing work or conflict with it, or it's already done, or it doesn't need it anymore." Add a Sweep: a button on the builds page (and API/voice: 'sweep the builds') plus an automatic run on every land. It checks every step of every pending and queued build against the Shipped features ledger, main's code, and the other pending/queued builds, and flags each step: Already done (shipped by build X), Conflicts (would change/break feature Y, shows the files and lines), Duplicate (same as a step in build Z), Obsolete (no longer needed: superseded or its target was removed), OK. Results: badges on each build and step, a Sweep report with a filter per flag, and one-tap fixes per flag: drop step, merge into the other build, move to Conflicts for Brett, keep. Nothing is changed without Brett's tap. Cheap first pass in plain code (ledger + file overlap); Claude only for the unclear ones.

Correction (Brett): the Sweep does NOT run automatically on every land. It runs only (1) when Brett runs it (button / API / voice), and (2) by the orchestrator on a single build at two points: when it receives the job, and again right before it dispatches it (launches the session). Flags found at dispatch hold the build for Brett instead of launching.

before.title: Every UI fully API-controllable: rule, CI parity check, audit, deep links
before.detail: Builds on full-api-control (unpushed branch claude/full-api-control: api-coverage@1 checker, control@1 console.values/elements, API Browser); merged in so both land as one PR. Adds plugin-view parity (open/state/actions/settings through named API, not only generic element presses), a deep link per plugin view, the audit, and full API for the Demonstration Designer and Book Builder.

origin.said:
Standing rule: anything with a UI must have API functions that can do everything the UI can (open, read state, every action, every setting). Voice control is the app's main selling point and rides on this.

1. Orchestrator: every brief it writes for a build that touches UI includes this requirement explicitly (brief template + brief writer). Keep it short.
2. CI check: every registered UI asset/control/plugin view maps to API operations covering its actions and settings; fail when missing; report gaps.
3. Audit: list every existing UI lacking full API coverage, starting with the glossary/index Demonstration Designer and Book Builder; fix those two here, add the rest as pending builds.
4. Deep link per plugin view (URL that opens it) so agents can open any UI on the phone.

before.title: Account health probe + failover + phone alerts
before.detail: A (new): probe every Claude account (subscriptions + API keys) on console load and on a schedule with a tiny headless session (no rules, no CLAUDE.md, no MCP): login valid, usage left (5-hour + weekly, resets; API balance/spend vs cap), models it can use. One shared account-status store every plugin reads (usage badge, Claude accounts screen, routing); routing only sends a job to an account the store says can take it with the model it needs. E: phone notification before and after the probe (type account-status). B/C/D are built by account-failover-notify (same branch line); this build stacks on it.

notes.text: Claude account: live (axf-account-health-failover--earl, own login copy)

origin.said: Account health probe + failover + phone alerts (Brett). A. Health probe (new): On console load and on a schedule, the orchestrator probes EVERY Claude account (subscriptions + API keys): a tiny headless session with a minimal brief, NO rules, NO CLAUDE.md, no MCP. It checks: login valid, credits/usage available (5-hour + weekly used/left, reset times; API: balance or last-known spend vs cap), which models it can use (opus/fable/etc.). It saves each account's status in ONE shared store all plugins read (status: ok / limited / no credits / login expired; credits left; models; checked at). Usage badge, Claude accounts screen and routing all read it. Keep probe cost near zero. The orchestrator only sends a job to an account that the store says can take it, with the model it needs. B. Failover: If a build still fails on auth or limit, mark the account out, update the store, and relaunch the same build on the next able account. Today 5 builds died in 1-3 s on account-1 (expired) and account-3 Hulu (no credits) and nothing retried. C. Phone alerts (AmberX): Notify on every account problem: which account, what (expired / limit / no credits), which build moved where, what Brett must do. D. One home per login: Each account's credentials live in exactly ONE store; every token refresh from any build/console/session writes back there. Audit claude-login.mjs, claude-token-save.mjs, claude-headless.sh, console AI keys for duplicate copies; find why account-1's refresh failed and report. Rules: Full API + voice + MCP/CLI control; settings in categorized collapsible sections (probe interval, alerts); tests; report, STATUS, THREADS. E. Probe notifications (Brett): When the console loads: send a phone notification that the account checks are about to run; when done, send another with the result per account (ok / limited / no credits / expired, credits left, models). Uses the AmberX notification panel (build amberx-notify-panel) as its type 'account-status'.

origin.said: AmberX notification panel (Brett): A real notification panel inside the AmberX phone app that receives every kind of notification and status from the console, orchestrator, axHub and builds. 1. Typed notifications: build started/done/failed, approvals and veto holds (with Deny / Run now), account status (checks starting/done, expired, limit, no credits), UI Review items, alerts, info. Extensible type registry. 2. Panel: list grouped by type/source, filters, unread counts, search, mark read, clear, pin; tap opens the related screen; action buttons per type. 3. Live status area: current account statuses, running builds, queue. 4. Also delivered as Android push notifications with actions; panel keeps history. 5. One send API every plugin uses (console, orchestrator, axHub); reuse existing notifications/alert hub code (notifications-control-panel groups/triggers/actions) where it exists. Rules: Full API + voice + MCP/CLI control; settings in categorized collapsible sections (per-type on/off, sound, priority); 3 UI options to UI Review; phone screenshots; tests; report, STATUS, THREADS.

before.title: Slot watchdog crew member (Slot Warden)
before.detail: Plain-code watchdog (zero tokens) on the headless build slots and queue: every ~30 s checks each running slot against reality (tmux alive, claude pid alive, log advancing); dead / finished / hung -> release slot, mark build failed with reason (auth, limit, crash, hung), tell the orchestrator, notify Brett (type slot). Live status + intervention log in console and AmberX. Root fix: claude-headless.sh always releases its slot when Claude exits. Duplicate guard on launch and in the watchdog (reuses orchestrator-dup-check). Crew member Slot Warden on the roster.

origin.said:
Assign a crew member (agent profile in the roster, e.g. a 'Slot Warden') whose only job is watching the headless build slots and queue, all the time, in plain code (zero tokens).

1. Every ~30 s: check each running slot in framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs against reality (tmux session alive, claude -p pid alive, log advancing). Today 3 builds died in 1-3 s on bad logins but kept all 3 slots, freezing the queue.
2. Dead / finished / hung (no log progress past a threshold) -> release the slot, mark the build failed with the reason (auth, limit, crash, hung), tell the orchestrator so it can relaunch/fail over (account-health-failover build), and notify Brett's phone (AmberX notification panel, type 'slot').
3. Report: a live slot/queue status the console and AmberX show; a log of every intervention.
4. Also fix the root: claude-headless.sh must always finish/release its slot when Claude exits, even on instant auth failure.

Duplicate guard (Brett): The watchdog and the launcher refuse or stop duplicate builds: same brief/goal running twice (e.g. memory-manager-r2 and -r3 both ran). On launch, compare against running + queued builds (name stem, brief source, build id); keep the furthest-along one, stop/dequeue the other, tell the orchestrator and notify Brett. Reuse the unlanded orchestrator-dup-check branch.

before.title: Demonstration Designer plugin (new, standalone)
before.detail: New standalone console plugin 'Demonstration Designer' (own nav entry), replacing the disabled glossary-index one. Brett found the old one unusable, so make it simple and obvious. Pick any screen, plugin or UI element from the live registry, then build a demo: steps (open screen, highlight, click/type action, wait), narration text + voice, captions, timing. Record a demo by doing it, edit it on a timeline, preview, play it live on the console or a sandboxed preview, export as video. Demos are saved assets, reusable and chainable into longer tours. Harvest useful code from the disabled glossary-index plugin (demos.mjs, walkthrough engine) instead of starting from zero. RULE: every UI action and setting has API + voice + MCP/CLI control, and a deep link opens it. Settings in categorized collapsible sections; 3 UI options to UI Review; tests; report.

notes.text: PURPOSE (Brett): it's for PITCHING the product. Keep it dead simple. Main flow = three picks: (1) plugin or topic, (2) length in minutes, (3) narrator voice; then ONE Generate button. Generate writes a pitch script (hook up front, benefits not specs, closing call to action), picks the best screens, and plays a polished demo on real data: highlights, smooth zooms/pans, captions, background music, logo intro/outro. before.detail: Contract work (Fable). New asset schemas for crew agents: agent-skill@1 (name, domain, what it does, tools allowed, files/areas it owns, rules, checks it runs, model preference, cost cap, examples) and agent-persona@1 (name, nickname, voice/tone, job title, avatar, how it reports, strengths, limits), plus agent-profile@1 that combines one persona with several skills. Validators, fixtures, CI check. Ship a large library of boilerplate templates: skills (React UI, Kotlin/Compose, Python server, plugin manifests, themes/skins, tests, docs, merge-fixer, CI fixer, slot watchdog, account health, notifications, voice/API wiring, security review, UI Review designer, demo/pitch writer, data/Postgres, deploy/Coolify, refactor, perf) and personas (lander, reviewer, builder, watchdog, reporter, etc.). Template picker + 'new from template' in the Crew plugin; migrate the existing roster (Earl, Rhonda, Sully, Lenny, Gina, Paulie, Joey, Vinnie) onto it. Orchestrator reads skills when assigning steps. Every UI gets full API + voice + MCP/CLI control. Settings in categorized collapsible sections; 3 UI options to UI Review; tests; report.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

(3) Drag-and-drop agent designer: drag skills, tools and a persona onto an agent card to build it. (4) ONE new Agent Manager interface that merges and REPLACES the existing agent/crew screens (skills, tools, personas, roster); remove the old UI (keep code for harvesting). Clean, nice design. (5) Include a RAG database: agents get a retrieval knowledge base (index docs/code/memory, embeddings, search) with RAG skills; manageable in the Agent Manager. Estimate grows accordingly; split into steps.

Brett: every employee is an agent and lives in the Agent Manager. One employee list = the agent list (whole roster, job titles, crew/ID cards, HR info), each with its persona, skills, tools and RAG knowledge. No separate crew/HR list elsewhere; Crew and HR views read this one list.

Drag any persona, tool or skill from the trees onto an agent to add it; drag between agents; multi-select drag.

> There's too many tables that show information about builds. Get rid of all of them. All we want is pending queued and built. All on one page in different tabs.

Brett said:
"There's too many tables that show information about builds. Get rid of all of them. All we want is pending queued and built. All on one page in different tabs."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine.
