origin.brief:
# Build: plan-studio-receives-a-valid-shipped-feature-man

## Brett said (verbatim)
> Make sure it creates the plant studio, make sure it gets all the, the correct information, the fields of the manifest are sent to the plant studio. So the plant studio's gotta receive a manifest too. It has to be valid.

## What to build
Continue build "Plan Studio receives a valid shipped-feature manifest" (plan-studio-receives-a-valid-shipped-feature-man) — Phase 2, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said:
"Make sure it creates the plant studio, make sure it gets all the, the correct information, the fields of the manifest are sent to the plant studio. So the plant studio's gotta receive a manifest too. It has to be valid."
This phase downgrades Fable → Opus: fine, no approval needed (it is recorded when you tick its first step).
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.

This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account account-3 for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step plan-studio-receives-a-valid-shipped-feature-man <stepId> done). before.detail: Today every orchestrator brief says 'read only the files listed' but lists no files. before.title: Headless loop guards: stop endless loops and searches
before.detail: Guards on every headless session the orchestrator launches (claude-headless.sh + agent-slots + the running-builds watchdog's afterTick hook in pipeline.mjs): 1) Hard caps per session: --max-turns, wall time and cost cap derived from the step estimates (e.g. 2x estimate), settings with defaults. 2) Step progress timer: no step tick within 1.5x the step's estimate -> warn note, at 2x -> stop the session, build back to pending with the reason. 3) Loop detector reading the live log: the same command/tool call (or near-identical grep/find/sed) repeated N times, or M searches in a row with no edit/commit -> stop and note. 4) Search budget per step (e.g. 15 greps/finds) written into the brief and enforced by the detector. 5) Every stop: build note with the reason and last log lines, AmberX notification (normal notification, not an alarm), slot released, no auto-relaunch of a looped step until Brett says. 6) Brief line: 'If you can't find something in 3 searches, stop and leave a note.' Settings in orchestrator settings (categorized sections), full API/MCP/CLI/voice control. Tests with fake logs: repeated command, search spree, no tick, cost cap.

notes.text: Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: "I need a way to manage the safeguards." Add a Safeguards panel (orchestrator settings, its own section, also reachable from the build's row): turn each guard on/off; edit turns cap, time cap (x estimate), cost cap, no-tick warn/stop multipliers, repeat-command count, search budget; per-build and per-queue overrides; a live view of each running session against its limits (turns, time, cost, searches used); a log of every guard stop with the reason, last log lines and buttons: Relaunch, Raise limit and relaunch, Send back to pending. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and a deep link. Stock controls, 3 layout options to UI Review.

Brett on managing the safeguards: "I don't want the file itself to be editable. I want it to be view. You can view the file with steps. Make it an MD file with bullet points for the rules. And create a sortable, collapsible tree with a whole shitload of different rules, of snippets. When you click it, it will pop a dialogue to let you add the custom fields that it requires for the snippet and it will insert it." Build: 1) The safeguards live as a Markdown rules file (one bullet per rule, grouped by heading), shown READ-ONLY in the panel (rendered view with the steps it applies to); no free-text editing. 2) A snippet library: a sortable, searchable, collapsible tree (category > sub-category > snippet) with a large set of ready rule snippets (turn caps, time/cost caps, no-tick timeouts, repeat-command and search-spree limits, file/folder fences, no sub-agents, model limits, test-before-commit, stop-and-note rules, etc.). 3) Clicking a snippet opens a dialog with the fields it needs (number, duration, $, path, model, scope: global/queue/build/step) with validation and a preview line; Insert adds the bullet to the rules file. 4) Each inserted rule can be toggled, moved, or removed from the panel (structured actions, still no raw edit); every change is versioned with history and undo. 5) The orchestrator and the loop detector read their limits from this file; the brief gets the bullets that apply to the step. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control; stock controls; 3 layout options to UI Review.

Brett: "the dialogue that needs custom parameters for the rules, any that are like file names or specific things already have a list to choose from for the custom parameters." In the snippet fields dialog, every field whose values already exist is a pick list (searchable dropdown or tree picker), not free text: file and folder paths (from the repo tree / plugin registry), plugins, apps, builds, queues, steps, Claude accounts, API accounts, models, agents/crew, tools, commands, settings keys. Multi-select where a rule takes several. Free text only for true free values (numbers, durations, $ amounts) and those get validated inputs with units.

Brett: "There has to be filters too, where you put in for the list of certain types of parameters. There's got to be filters." Every pick list in the snippet dialog has filters fitting its type, plus search: files/folders by app, plugin, folder, file type/extension, changed recently, owned by a build; plugins by app, category, enabled; builds by status, queue, model, category, date; queues by account type; steps by build and state; accounts by role, model available, health; models by tier; agents by role/skill; tools by service; settings keys by plugin/section. Filters combine, show counts, can be cleared, and remember the last used per field.

Brett: "list of features. Stack. And the list of predefined search terms based on what the rule is." 1) Filters stack (combine) and include a 'feature' filter: pick from the Shipped features list / plugin feature catalog to narrow files, builds and steps to one feature. 2) Each snippet carries predefined search terms and preset filter stacks that fit that rule (e.g. a file-fence rule offers 'server routes', 'web views', 'plugin.json', 'tests', 'schemas'; a model rule offers 'Fable-only steps', 'UI steps'), shown as quick chips in the pick list; tap one to apply. Brett can save his own presets per snippet.

Brett: "as you type in the field, it automatically drops down the list of all the ones that match. Whatever you type. In real time. Letter per letter." Every parameter field is a type-ahead combobox: the match list drops down on the first letter and updates on every keystroke (fuzzy match, matched letters highlighted, within the active filters), keyboard up/down/enter and tap to pick. Fast on large lists (indexed/virtualized, no lag).

Brett: "And they pop up in a categorized tree." The live type-ahead drop-down shows its matches as a categorized collapsible tree (e.g. app > plugin > folder > file; queue > build > step; account type > account), branches with matches auto-expand, counts per branch, empty branches hidden; picking a branch can select all under it where the rule allows several.

before.title: Shipped Features: live manifests from dispatch to done, badges + progress meter
before.detail: Builds on shipped-manifest-api (landed 79ed472c0f1f, shipped-manifest@1). Today the manifest is sent only when a build lands. Change: the orchestrator sends a manifest to Shipped Features (and Plan Studio, per the queued Plan Studio manifest build) at every event: when it dispatches the job, on every build update (model/account change, note, hold, guard stop), on every step completed, and on completion/land. Each manifest is versioned (sequence number, previous version kept as history) and validated. The Shipped Features entry exists from dispatch, not only after landing, and shows a live status badge (dispatched, building, step x/y, waiting on UI Review, held, stopped by guard, failed, landed, shipped) plus a progress meter (steps done / total, time and cost used vs estimate), updated in real time (live push, no refresh). History view per entry shows every manifest. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep link. Tests: dispatch creates the entry, each step tick bumps the version and meter, land sets shipped; invalid manifest is refused with the reason.

notes.text: Brett: "it lists what files were touched too, but they're hidden... in a collapsible, in an expanded row... you gotta expand a few things to get to them. Clicking it opens a dialog with the file list; clicking a file opens it in a read-only code editor (syntax highlight, diff vs before toggle). Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: "when you open the file, it will jump to the feature that you found it through and highlight it. In focus, centered in screen." The manifest records, per touched file, the line ranges each step/feature changed. Brett: "Any failed, any errors that are file related get sent to the log with links to the file with the bad code there, the conflicted code, and highlighted and in focus." Brett: "also make an errors column that's hideable. With a collapse button." Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control.

Brett: prompt field to jump into a headless session. A running claude -p can't take input, so: a prompt field (on the build's Shipped Features entry, the Errors column line, and the session window) that, on send, does NOT send right away: it opens a confirm dialog warning that the running session will be stopped and any unfinished, uncommitted work in progress may be lost, showing what's at risk (current step, uncommitted files count, time/cost so far). Only on Confirm: stop the session cleanly (let it commit if it can), then resume the SAME session (claude --resume <session id>) with Brett's prompt so its context is kept; logged as a build note and a manifest update. Cancel keeps the prompt as a draft. Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control, with the same confirm step.

before.title: UI Roller: roll a random style on any UI element
before.detail: New UI Roller plugin (console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web; every app built on the framework). 1) Context menu on EVERY UI element (dialogs, windows, panels, bars, buttons, inputs, menus, text, widgets; all registry assets): 'Roll style' and, when the element has a roll, 'Reset element'. 2) 'Roll style' opens a dialog: checkboxes for what to roll (colours, typography, spacing/density, size, radius/shape, borders, shadows, motion, icons), optional scope (this element / all of its type / its plugin), live preview, Re-roll, Apply. Rolls stay within valid token ranges and keep contrast readable. Apply saves the result as asset token overrides (local-first, like other overrides). 3) Main Settings > Rolled assets page: lists every app and plugin with its rolled assets (tree, counts, filters, search); each shows a live preview of the asset and its roll; actions: Reset (one), Reset selected (multi-select), Reset all. Undo/history per roll. 4) Applying a skin, design pack or theme clears EVERY rolled asset: covered ones take the new look, all others go back to their defaults. 5) Full API/MCP/CLI/voice control and deep links for roll, reset, reset selected/all and the page. Stock framework controls; 3 layout options to UI Review; tests (roll writes tokens, reset restores, theme apply clears all rolls); report.

before.title: URGENT: approval links say 'Method not allowed'
before.detail: Approval links sent in notices and by Claude (https://axhub.amberxai.com/auth/admin/approvals/<id>) answer 'Method not allowed' when Brett taps Approve. Land it the same day.

before.title: Reserve build IDs at once: add returns the ID with the veto countdown
before.detail: Today pending_change add (and control_add on planner.builds/plans) is held on the 90 s veto countdown and the orchestrator only assigns the build ID when it runs, so callers (Claude sessions) must guess the ID from the title to add notes. Fix: the orchestrator (ID registry) reserves the ID the moment the call arrives, before the hold, and returns it in the held result (e.g. reservedId). Notes, sub prompts and status calls on a reserved ID queue up and apply in order once the add runs; if Brett denies the add, the reservation and anything queued on it are dropped. IDs never collide (registry check). Same for plan_park and plan_add. Tests: add returns the id while held; a note on the reserved id lands after the add; deny drops both.

before.title: Permissions control panel: every axHub tool's policy in one place
before.detail: Repo: axHub (policy store) + console/axhub-web screen. One Permissions panel listing every connected service and every tool (vps.build_start, vps.run, axf-console.*, github, hostinger, amberx...) with its policy (allow / veto countdown / confirm / deny), countdown length, who may call it (Brett's sessions, Claude sessions, headless builds, agents), and passes. Brett changes a policy with a dropdown; bulk change per service or by filter (destructive, writes, reads). Tree grouped by service > category, search, filters, live type-ahead. Every change logged with history and undo. Claude sessions and builds can read policies but never change them (owner-only, enforced on the hub, not just the UI). First change: set vps.build_start to deny so only the orchestrator launches builds. Full API (read for all, write owner-only), voice for Brett. 3 layout options to UI Review.

notes.text: Brett: "Can I make it so that employees like Molly or Amber or Moses can use it, and then I assign one of the employees to the orchestrator so the orchestrator can say run it, change it?" Permissions are granted per employee (agent from the one roster: Molly, Amber, Moses, Brownie, etc.), not just per session type. Brett assigns an employee to the orchestrator; the orchestrator acts with that employee's permissions. Brett can grant an employee permission to change policies, but only within a ceiling Brett sets: an employee can never raise its own or another's permissions above the ceiling, never touch owner-only settings or the ceiling itself, every change it makes is logged with the employee's name and sends Brett a notification, and Brett can revoke instantly. Panel shows per-employee view and per-tool view.

before.title: Session transcripts API: search what was said, find which session
before.detail: Builds on ui-review-notify-session-audio (landed Nov 7): sessions are recorded by AmberX's Audio Output Recorder (output-recorder plugin) and transcribed by the faster-whisper worker, transcripts saved on the hub, readable in the recorder page. Today output-recorder's plugin.json declares no transcript commands, so nothing outside the page can read them. Add full API (plugin-commands@1, so MCP/axHub, REST, CLI, voice come for free): list sessions with transcripts (date, length, linked Claude session, title); read one transcript (whole or a time range, with timestamps); search across all transcripts (words or phrase, date range, fuzzy), returning the matching session, timestamp, a few lines of context, and a deep link that opens the recorder page at that moment (and plays the audio there). Also a 'find the session where we talked about X' command that ranks sessions by match. Reachable from Claude chat/voice sessions through axHub so Claude or Gizmo can answer 'which session did we talk about this'. Read-only; respects the recorder's settings. Tests; report.

notes.text: Brett: "I can find that internally without AI, right?" Yes: all search is plain code with zero tokens (full-text index over the transcripts, phrase + fuzzy + date filters). Add a search box with live type-ahead results on the recorder page and in the console's Search everything, so Brett can find a session himself without any AI. Claude/Gizmo only call the same plain search through the API.
Split by rules (Claude: claude exit 1: Error: Input must be provided either through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print): one step per line of the request, review the steps.

Brett: results pop up in a scrolling window. As Brett types in Search everything (or the recorder page), matching transcript snippets pop up live in a scrolling results window: each hit shows the session (date, title), timestamp and a few lines around the match with the words highlighted; infinite scroll, grouped by session, newest first with a sort switch. Tapping a hit opens the recorder at that moment and plays the audio. Plain search also drops filler phrases like 'find the session where', 'when we talked about' so a whole sentence still works, zero tokens.

Brett: "With the keywords in focus." In the scrolling results window each snippet is centered on the matched keywords, highlighted. Opening a hit scrolls the transcript so the keyword is centered on screen, highlighted and focused, with next/previous match buttons inside that session.

Brett: "there's a column on the left with all the hits. All the sessions that match: the session name and the type of thing we were talking about." Results window layout: left column lists every session with hits (session name, date, hit count, and a topic tag for what it was about, e.g. builds, skins, approvals, AmberX); tapping one shows its hits on the right, keywords centered and highlighted. Topic tags: from the linked Claude session's title and the builds it touched (plain code, zero tokens); optionally a cheap one-time tag per session after transcription, off by default.

Brett: "I want a RAG database made of all the transcripts." Build a RAG store over every transcript: chunk each transcript (with session, date, timestamps, speaker, topic tags), embed the chunks with a local embedding model on the VPS (no Claude tokens), store them in Postgres with pgvector (reuse the postgres-console container plan if it exists, else its own table), and index every new transcript automatically after transcription. Two ways in: 1) semantic search (meaning, not just exact words) in the same results window, mixed with the keyword hits; 2) 'Ask' (API/MCP/voice): Claude or Gizmo retrieve the top chunks and answer with the sessions and timestamps as sources, each linking to that moment. Share the store with the Agent Manager's RAG knowledge (agent-profile build) so employees can use it. Settings: on/off, re-index, what gets indexed. Tests: retrieval returns the right session for a paraphrased question.

origin.said: I want the API to be able to access the transcript so I can tell you or I can tell Gizmo, you know, what session was it that we talked about this or that.

before.title: Fix: stale running counts per Claude account not cleared
before.detail: Seen Nov 9: claude_accounts shows Hulu 1/3, Moses X 4/3, account-1 4/3 running while the VPS has 0 tmux axf-* sessions and 0 claude -p processes. Rule (Brett): every time the console loads, and on the watchdog tick, the orchestrator checks for stale runs and releases any slot or running entry with no live process (agent-slots, claude-workers.mjs counts, orchestrator.json statuses). Find why the existing check didn't run or didn't clear these; fix; add a test with fake stale entries; log each release.

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.

before.title: Fix: stale running counts per Claude account not cleared
before.detail: Seen Nov 9: claude_accounts shows Hulu 1/3, Moses X 4/3, account-1 4/3 running while the VPS has 0 tmux axf-* sessions and 0 claude -p processes. Rule (Brett): every time the console loads, and on the watchdog tick, the orchestrator checks for stale runs and releases any slot or running entry with no live process (agent-slots, claude-workers.mjs counts, orchestrator.json statuses). Find why the existing check didn't run or didn't clear these; fix; add a test with fake stale entries; log each release.

notes.text: ROOT CAUSE (found live): deploy/claude-workers.mjs liveSessions() runs `tmux ls`; when NO tmux sessions exist, tmux exits non-zero ('no server running'), so it returns null = 'can't ask tmux'. Then ledger() counts every open session as running and liveClaims keeps claims for 12 h. So the stale entries survive exactly when nothing is running. Fix: treat 'no server running' (tmux present, exit 1) as an empty Set; only return null when tmux binary is missing. Test it.

origin.brief:
# Build: orchestrator-self-check-when-stuck-verify-each-a

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-09T16:25:52.442Z
> The orchestrator is supposed to check all that every time it loads if things are stuck. If he has any problems, he's supposed to check each account one by one. And look for stale jobs.

## What to build
Continue build "Orchestrator self-check when stuck: verify each account one by one, clear stale jobs" (orchestrator-self-check-when-stuck-verify-each-a) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-09 16:25):
"The orchestrator is supposed to check all that every time it loads if things are stuck. If he has any problems, he's supposed to check each account one by one. And look for stale jobs."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) On every load and whenever the queue is stuck (e.g. 'no Claude account is signed in on the VPS' while accounts are actually signed in), the orchestrator checks each saved account one by one (subscription logins and API keys: signed in, limited, key valid, slots), rebuilds its account list, and reaps stale jobs/running counts with no live process. Log what it found and fixed; notify AmberX. Fold in pending builds fix-stale-running-counts-per-claude-account-not-cleared and real-time-slot-tracking-stale-data-reaper where they overlap.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) The orchestrator is supposed to check all that every time it loads if things are stuck. If he has any problems, he's supposed to check each account one by one. And look for stale jobs.
[ ] s3 (~20 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/orchestrator-self-check-when-stuck-verify-each-a.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/orchestrator-self-check-when-stuck-verify-each-a.md, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step orchestrator-self-check-when-stuck-verify-each-a <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link orchestrator-self-check-when-stuck-verify-each-a --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account account-3 for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step orchestrator-self-check-when-stuck-verify-each-a <stepId> done). When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. Simplify appearance to two concepts: skins (look, style, layout, behaviour of every asset) and colour themes. 1) Convert every existing design pack (design-package / style-package assets, Design packs screen picks) into a skin so nothing is lost. 2) Remove the Design packs screen, settings, menu entries and asset types (design-package, style-package), redirect old references to skins. 3) Appearance settings shows only Skin and Colour theme pickers. Check if style-theme / layout themes should also fold into skins and list it in the report for Brett, don't remove those without asking. Default look must stay identical; screenshots to UI Review.

origin.brief:
# Build: account-failover-chain-subscription-next-subscri

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-09T17:44:47.652Z
> The orchestrator assigns a model; if it doesn't work, it goes to another subscription, and if there's no subscriptions, it goes to an API. Whatever account or API actually does the job, the orchestrator notes it: this account is the one who built it.

## What to build
Continue build "Account failover chain: subscription, next subscription, then API; record who actually built it" (account-failover-chain-subscription-next-subscri) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-09 17:44):
"The orchestrator assigns a model; if it doesn't work, it goes to another subscription, and if there's no subscriptions, it goes to an API. Whatever account or API actually does the job, the orchestrator notes it: this account is the one who built it."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) When the orchestrator launches a step on its chosen account and the login fails or is limited, it marks that account limited and retries on the next subscription account in priority order; if no subscription can run it, it goes to an API-key account under its caps. Whichever account or API key actually ran the step is recorded on the step and build (account, email, model, cost) and shown in the orchestrator. Never silently fall back outside this chain. - Pending: no timer; created date, steps, priority, Send to orchestrator.
- Queued: queue position, why it's waiting, account/model planned.
- Active: animated activity indicator in the row, live elapsed timer, steps complete with progress bar, current step, account actually running it.
- Complete: started/finished dates, duration, cost, account that actually built it, PR/land status.

## What to build
Continue build "Prompt caching and Batch API support in the build orchestrator" (prompt-caching-and-batch-api-support-in-the-buil) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-09 16:02):

# Build: right-click-a-queued-build-to-assign-it-to-a-spe

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-09T16:03:35.870Z
> I need to be able to right-click jobs in the orchestrator and assign them to one of my stored accounts.

## What to build
Continue build "Right-click a queued build to assign it to a specific saved Claude account" (right-click-a-queued-build-to-assign-it-to-a-spe) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-09 16:03):
"I need to be able to right-click jobs in the orchestrator and assign them to one of my stored accounts."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) In the orchestrator's Pending/Queue/Building tables, add a right-click menu on a build to pick any saved account (subscription logins and API-key accounts, e.g. Hulu, Moses X, Moses X API) or Auto. Dispatcher honors the pinned account: waits for its slot, respects API daily/weekly caps, shows the pinned account on the row. Also allow changing it while queued. Expose the same as a control command for voice.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) I need to be able to right-click jobs in the orchestrator and assign them to one of my stored accounts.

Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). # Build: test-button-on-every-claude-account-subscription

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-09T20:16:02.957Z
> Why is there no way to test these accounts? There's no fucking button to test them.

## Addendum 1 (Brett (voice))
> When this page opens, it needs to have an animation, an animated thing saying it's loading as it checks each account one at a time and shows their status.
## Addendum 2 (Brett (voice))
> I only want it to check the accounts once. When the console opens for the first time and nothing is running.

## What to build
Continue build "Test button on every Claude account (subscription and API)" (test-button-on-every-claude-account-subscription) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-09 20:16):
"Why is there no way to test these accounts? There's no fucking button to test them."
Addendum 1: "When this page opens, it needs to have an animation, an animated thing saying it's loading as it checks each account one at a time and shows their status."
Addendum 2: "I only want it to check the accounts once. When the console opens for the first time and nothing is running."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. [ ] s1 (~30 min) Claude accounts page (Settings > Plugins > Claude accounts) and Job routing: a Test button on every account row that runs a tiny no-tool check with that account's saved login or API key (no AI build, minimal tokens) and shows alive / expired login / bad key / out of credits / limit hit, which models it can run (Opus, Fable), and when it was last checked. before.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
before.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

before.title: Saved Claude logins never end up on a spent refresh token
before.detail: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.

steps.text: Builds run on a per-build copy of a saved login (claude-login.mjs). Refresh tokens are single-use: when a build refreshes, the new token lands in the copy; if the copy is deleted before the rotation is written back (claude-token-save.mjs release/sweep), the saved login keeps a spent token and every later launch fails with 'OAuth session expired and could not be refreshed' (seen on account-1 and account-3, Nov 9). Fix: find every path where the rotation is lost (crash, kill, exit 1, sweep timing, two builds refreshing the same login at once), write rotations back atomically with a lock, never let two copies refresh the same login concurrently, and before launch check the saved login is alive; if dead, skip that account, alert the phone, and don't burn runs on it. Tests for each path.
Why is it expiring when it gets a new refresh token every time? ... Okay, we need to do something about that so it doesn't happen.

before.detail: Today the orchestrator's dispatcher keeps its own account list and API settings (pipeline-settings: apiOverflow, apiAccounts, its own account records), separate from Claude accounts (deploy/claude-workers.mjs, workers.json: accounts, roles, API workers, caps, Job routing rules, 'API fallback when subscriptions are busy'). So the orchestrator didn't see Hulu API or the fallback Gizmo turned on. Fix: Claude accounts / workers.json is the single source of truth for accounts, models per account, API workers, caps, fallback and routing rules. The orchestrator reads it live and keeps no copy; remove the duplicate settings (migrate any values), and show the same account status in both places.

# Build: per-account-queues-long-press-a-queued-build-to

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-09T20:26:06.899Z
> I want to be able to hold a job down in the build manager or in the orchestrator in the queue and send it to an API immediately. An API queue. I want every account to have its own queue.

## What to build
Continue build "Per-account queues + long-press a queued build to send it to an API account now" (per-account-queues-long-press-a-queued-build-to) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-09 20:26):
"I want to be able to hold a job down in the build manager or in the orchestrator in the queue and send it to an API immediately. An API queue. I want every account to have its own queue."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Every Claude account (subscription and API) gets its own queue in the orchestrator and the Build Manager, showing what's waiting and running on it. 2) Long-press (hold) a build in Pending or the Queue to get a menu to send it to any account's queue, including an API account's queue (e.g. Hulu API), so it starts there right away, still under the API caps. Drag between account queues too. Full API control per standing rule.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) I want to be able to hold a job down in the build manager or in the orchestrator in the queue and send it to an API immediately. An API queue. I want every account to have its own queue.
[ ] s3 (~20 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/per-account-queues-long-press-a-queued-build-to.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR

Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link per-account-queues-long-press-a-queued-build-to --branch <b> --pr <n>.

Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

Fix: Claude accounts / workers.json is the single source of truth for accounts, models per account, API workers, caps, fallback and routing rules. The orchestrator reads it live and keeps no copy; remove the duplicate settings (migrate any values), and show the same account status in both places.

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Skins restyle EVERYTHING: badges, banner and every visual element" (skins-restyle-everything-badges-banner-and-every-visual-element) [Appearance] — Phase 2, model Fable.
This phase upgrades Opus → Fable: no approval needed (Fable upgrades need my approval is off); it is recorded when you tick its first step.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Branch: claude/skins-restyle-everything-badges-banner-and-every-visual-element · PR #409
Steps in this phase (1 left, ~30 min):
[ ] s6 (~30 min) Add skin entries in asset-types.json for all 44 uncovered types: color-theme, style-theme, layout, app-menu, toolbar, nav-menu, context-menu, tab-group, dialog, popup, button, slider, container, gauge, meter, banner, clock, search-bar, action-button, logo, label, status, counter, progress, avatar, link, theme-switch, spacer, divider, badge, settings, dock-layout, xlayout, nav-style, behavior-theme, branding, typography, density, sizing, agent-card, demonstration, book, clip, docs. Types that ARE skin ingredients (themes, typography, density, sizing) get an explicit exclusion instead. Additive only: default skin must look identical (before/after screenshot diff). Do this BEFORE enabling the CI gate so open PRs aren't blocked. Also (engine, Fable): an optional `text` selector list on schemas/customize.json targets, drawn by customizeCss with the type's text parts, so text children that keep their own look (.fx-banner__logo, .fx-nav__header, .fx-card__head; see framework/spec/SKIN-AUDIT.md shadowed) follow the skin; default look unchanged.
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step skins-restyle-everything-badges-banner-and-every-visual-element <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link skins-restyle-everything-badges-banner-and-every-visual-element --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

And the demo can change the voice during playback, change the playback speed, you can hide certain things...

after.title: Failed launches auto-retry on another working account + re-run every build that died on login/credits
after.detail: Upgrades account-failover-chain-subscription-next-subscri (which itself died on account-1's expired login); don't duplicate it. 1) When a build session dies on an expired login, out of credits or a usage limit, the orchestrator marks that account (login-dead, or out until the reset time) and immediately re-launches the same build on the next working account: subscriptions first, then API overflow (account-5) within its cap. It keeps going until one works. No build stays failed for an account reason. 2) If a step was half done, it resumes from the last ticked step, not from scratch. 3) Model fallback: if the pinned model (e.g. Fable) is out everywhere, it waits for the reset or runs on Opus if allowed, and says which it did. 4) Every retry is logged in the fix log and Activity Monitor, with an FYI notification. Brett is told only when every account is exhausted, with the exact time of the next reset. 5) Right now, re-queue every build that died on a login or credits failure: skins-theme-rule, skins-restyle-finish, skins-own-everything-colour-theme-swaps-independ, appearance-skins-colour-themes-only-remove-design-packs, account-failover-chain, file-watchdog, home-page-build-queue-card, let-voice-api-route, orchestrator-and-build-manager-search-bar, prompt-caching, split-builds-pages (both), test-button-on-every-claude-account, urgent-terminal-pops-up, vps-orchestrator-only-rule, amberx-floating-toolbar. Put them on Moses X and account-5 now.

after.title: Skins as packages of slices: every section its own asset, pick sections on apply, mix creates a new skin via dialog, drag-and-drop Skin Builder
after.detail: Upgrade the existing skins/appearance system and asset registry; don't build a parallel one. 1) DATA MODEL: a skin is only a package (manifest) referencing section assets. Every section (colours, layouts, design/visual styles, behaviour, and every other category a skin covers) is its own standalone asset with a name, preview, tags and source. Convert every existing skin into this form, with no monolithic skins left. 2) APPLY WITH PICKS: when you apply, enable or change a skin, a dialog lists its sections with checkboxes and previews. Choose which sections to take and which to leave out; left-out sections keep the current skin's. 3) MIX = NEW SKIN: if the result mixes sections from more than one skin, a dialog asks you to save it as a new skin (name, description, thumbnail auto-captured), with Save as new, Apply without saving, or Cancel. 4) SKIN BUILDER: a slice library (searchable, by category, live hover preview) and a pack template with one slot per category. Drag slices into slots, preview the whole console live, see which slots are empty, swap or clear slots, before/after toggle. Save, apply, export or import as a file, duplicate, edit later. 5) Professional polish: snap animations, slot highlights, desktop and phone layouts. 6) Full control via REST, MCP, CLI and voice (list sections, save section, apply with includes/excludes, build skin from sections, export). Screenshots go to UI Review grouped by screen.

origin.said: For each section in skins, like colors, layouts, design, behavior, you need to be able to save each individual section as a new asset, then build your skins with these assets. origin.brief:
# Build: real-time-slot-tracking-stale-data-reaper

## Brett said (verbatim)
> 

## What to build
Continue build "Real-time slot tracking + stale data reaper" (real-time-slot-tracking-stale-data-reaper) [new feature] — Phase 1, model Opus.
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.

before.title: Account failover chain: subscription, next subscription, then API; record who actually built it
before.detail: When the orchestrator launches a step on its chosen account and the login fails or is limited, it marks that account limited and retries on the next subscription account in priority order; if no subscription can run it, it goes to an API-key account under its caps. Whichever account or API key actually ran the step is recorded on the step and build (account, email, model, cost) and shown in the orchestrator. Never silently fall back outside this chain. Builds on fix-account-attribution (running now, which records the real login) and overlaps pending running-builds-follow-the-active-claude-account-fail-over-when-it-dies and auto-switch-claude-account-when-the-active-one-r: fold them in.

## What to build
Continue build "Failed launches auto-retry on another working account + re-run every build that died on login/credits" (failed-launches-auto-retry-on-another-working-ac) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 00:19):
"When shit needs a rerun, rerun it. Find one that works. The orchestrator knows. It shouldn't just fail. It should find a new one and try it. Somebody else."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.

before.title: Account failover chain: subscription, next subscription, then API; record who actually built it
before.detail: When the orchestrator launches a step on its chosen account and the login fails or is limited, it marks that account limited and retries on the next subscription account in priority order; if no subscription can run it, it goes to an API-key account under its caps. Whichever account or API key actually ran the step is recorded on the step and build (account, email, model, cost) and shown in the orchestrator. Never silently fall back outside this chain. Builds on fix-account-attribution (running now, which records the real login) and overlaps pending running-builds-follow-the-active-claude-account-fail-over-when-it-dies and auto-switch-claude-account-when-the-active-one-r: fold them in.
